title.zh: 卷六十九 志第四十五 選舉一
title.raw: 卷六十九 志第四十五 選舉一 Volume 69 Treatises 45: Selection of Officials 1

sentences.zh: 選舉之法，大略有四：曰學校，曰科目，曰薦舉，曰銓選。

translations.literal: The methods of selection and recruitment, in broad outline, are four: namely schools, examinations, recommendation, and evaluation and appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The systems for recruiting officials fell, in broad terms, into four categories: state schools, civil examinations, recommendation, and evaluation and appointment.

sentences.zh: 學校以教育之，科目以登進之，薦舉以旁招之，銓選以佈列之，天下人才盡於是矣。

translations.literal: Schools used them for education, examinations for advancement, recommendation for recruitment from other channels, evaluation and appointment for arraying them in office—thus were all the talents under Heaven gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Schools trained them, examinations promoted them, recommendation drew talent from outside the regular channels, and evaluation and appointment placed them in office—through these four paths the empire gathered its men of ability.

sentences.zh: 明制，科目為盛，卿相皆由此出，學校則儲才以應科目者也。

translations.literal: Under the Ming system, examinations were paramount; ministers and chancellors all emerged from this route, while schools stored talent to supply the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Ming institutional order, the examination track dominated: chancellors and chief ministers rose through it, and the schools existed chiefly to stock candidates for those examinations.

sentences.zh: 其徑由學校通籍者，亦科目之亞也，外此則雜流矣。

translations.literal: Those who gained registry through the school route were also a subordinate form of the examination track; beyond this were the miscellaneous routes.
translations.idiomatic: Men who entered official registers through the schools ranked just below the examination path; everything outside that was classed as miscellaneous recruitment.

sentences.zh: 然進士、舉貢、雜流三途並用，雖有畸重，無偏廢也。

translations.literal: Yet the three routes of jinshi, presented tribute scholars, and miscellaneous streams were all employed together; though one might be disproportionately favored, none was wholly abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: All the same, jinshi graduates, tribute-presented scholars, and miscellaneous entrants were used side by side; one route might outweigh the others, but none was entirely set aside.

sentences.zh: 薦舉盛於國初，後因專用科目而罷。

translations.literal: Recommendation flourished at the founding of the state, but was later abolished because examinations alone were used.
translations.idiomatic: Recommendation was prominent in the dynasty's early years, then fell away once recruitment relied exclusively on the examinations.

sentences.zh: 銓選則入官之始，舍此蔑由焉。

translations.literal: Evaluation and appointment were the beginning of entering office; apart from this there was no other way.
translations.idiomatic: Evaluation and appointment marked the threshold of office; without them one could not enter the bureaucracy at all.

sentences.zh: 是四者釐然具載其本末，而二百七十年間取士得失之故可睹已。

translations.literal: These four are set forth clearly with their origins and outcomes, so that the reasons for success and failure in recruiting scholars over two hundred and seventy years may be seen.
translations.idiomatic: These four systems are recorded here in full sequence, so that the gains and losses in recruiting talent across the dynasty's two hundred and seventy years may be understood.

sentences.zh: 科舉必由學校，而學校起家，可不由科舉。

translations.literal: The examinations necessarily passed through the schools, yet one who rose through the schools might not necessarily pass through the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Civil examinations required schooling, yet men who entered office through the schools did not always have to take the examinations.

sentences.zh: 學校有二：曰國學，曰府、州、縣學。

translations.literal: There were two kinds of schools: the National Academy, and the prefectural, departmental, and county schools.
translations.idiomatic: Schools were of two kinds: the National Academy and the prefectural, departmental, and county schools.

sentences.zh: 府、州、縣學諸生入國學者，乃可得官，不入者不能得也。

translations.literal: Only students from prefectural, departmental, and county schools who entered the National Academy could obtain office; those who did not enter could not.
translations.idiomatic: Only local students who advanced to the National Academy could receive appointments; those who never entered could not.

sentences.zh: 入國學者，通謂之監生。

translations.literal: Those who entered the National Academy were generally called Directorate students.
translations.idiomatic: Students enrolled in the National Academy were known collectively as Directorate students (jiànshēng).

sentences.zh: 舉人曰舉監，生員曰貢監，品官子弟曰廕監，捐貲曰例監。

translations.literal: Provincial graduates were called examination Directorate students, student members tribute Directorate students, sons of ranked officials yin Directorate students, and those who paid contributions example Directorate students.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial graduates became "examination" Directorate students; local student members became "tribute" Directorate students; sons of ranked officials became "yin" Directorate students; and those who bought entry became "purchase" Directorate students.

sentences.zh: 同一貢監也，有歲貢，有選貢，有恩貢，有納貢。

translations.literal: Even within tribute Directorate students there were annual tribute, selected tribute, grace tribute, and purchased tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute Directorate students themselves were further divided into annual, selected, grace, and purchased tribute categories.

sentences.zh: 同一廕監也，有官生，有恩生。

translations.literal: Even within yin Directorate students there were official sons and grace sons.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Directorate students likewise split into regular official sons and grace sons.

sentences.zh: 國子學之設自明初乙巳始。

translations.literal: The establishment of the Directorate of the Sons of the State began in the yisi year at the beginning of Ming.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of the Sons of the State was first established in the yisi year of the dynasty's founding era.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年令品官子弟及民俊秀通文義者，並充學生。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongwu it was ordered that sons of ranked officials and outstanding commoners versed in literary meaning should all serve as students.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 1 (1368) the throne ordered that sons of ranked officials and talented commoners who understood classical texts should all enroll as students.

sentences.zh: 選國琦、王璞等十餘人，侍太子讀書禁中。

translations.literal: More than ten men including Guo Qi and Wang Pu were selected to attend the heir apparent in study within the Forbidden City.
translations.idiomatic: More than a dozen men, including Guo Qi and Wang Pu, were chosen to study with the heir apparent inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 入對謹身殿，姿狀明秀，應對詳雅。

translations.literal: They entered audience in the Hall of Scrupulous Conduct; their bearing was bright and refined, their responses detailed and elegant.
translations.idiomatic: When they were received in the Hall of Scrupulous Conduct, their bearing was bright and graceful and their replies thorough and polished.

sentences.zh: 太祖喜，因厚賜之。

translations.literal: The Taizu was pleased and therefore rewarded them generously.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor was delighted and bestowed rich rewards on them.

sentences.zh: 天下既定，詔擇府、州、縣學諸生入國子學。

translations.literal: When the realm was settled, an edict ordered that students from prefectural, departmental, and county schools be selected to enter the Directorate of the Sons of the State.
translations.idiomatic: Once the realm was pacified, an edict directed that outstanding students from local schools be chosen for the Imperial Directorate.

sentences.zh: 又擇年少舉人趙惟一等及貢生董昶等入學讀書，賜以衣帳，命於諸司先習吏事，謂之曆事監生。

translations.literal: Young provincial graduates such as Zhao Wei-yi and tribute graduates such as Dong Chang were also selected to enter and study; they were given clothing and bedding, and ordered to practice administrative affairs in the various offices first—these were called service-training Directorate students.
translations.idiomatic: Young provincial graduates such as Zhao Wei-yi and tribute scholars such as Dong Chang were likewise enrolled, given robes and bedding, and sent to government offices to learn administrative practice—they were called service-training Directorate students.

sentences.zh: 取其中尤英敏者李擴等入文華、武英堂說書，謂之小秀才。

translations.literal: The most exceptionally keen among them, such as Li Kuo, were taken into the Wenhua and Wuying halls to lecture on the classics—these were called junior xiucai.
translations.idiomatic: The brightest among them, such as Li Kuo, were assigned to lecture in the Wenhua and Wuying halls and were called "junior xiucai."

sentences.zh: 其才學優贍、聰明俊偉之士，使之博極羣書，講明道德經濟之學，以期大用，謂之老秀才。

translations.literal: Those of superior talent and learning, intelligence and stature, were made to master all books broadly and expound the learning of moral principle and statecraft, in expectation of great employment—these were called senior xiucai.
translations.idiomatic: Men of outstanding ability were set to master the full corpus of learning, to study moral philosophy and statecraft in depth, and to be groomed for high office—they were called "senior xiucai."

sentences.zh: 初，改應天府學為國子學，後改建於雞鳴山下。

translations.literal: At first the Yingtian Prefecture school was converted into the Directorate of the Sons of the State; later it was rebuilt at the foot of Jiming Hill.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Yingtian prefectural school became the Directorate; later the institution was rebuilt below Jiming Hill.

sentences.zh: 既而改學為監，設祭酒、司業及監丞、博士、助教、學正、學錄、典籍、掌饌、典簿等官。

translations.literal: Thereafter the school was changed to a Directorate, and offices were established for the libationer, vice-director, directorate assistant, erudites, assistants, rectifiers, recorders, archivists, provisioners, and registrars.
translations.idiomatic: The school was then renamed a Directorate, with posts for libationer, vice-director, assistant directors, erudites, teaching assistants, rectifiers, recorders, archivists, provisioners, and registrars.

sentences.zh: 分六堂以館諸生，曰率性、修道、誠心、正義、崇志、廣業。

translations.literal: Six halls were divided to lodge the students, named Following Nature, Cultivating the Way, Sincere Heart, Upright Principle, Elevating Aspiration, and Broadening Work.
translations.idiomatic: Students were housed in six halls: Following Nature, Cultivating the Way, Sincere Heart, Upright Principle, Elevating Aspiration, and Broadening Work.

sentences.zh: 學旁以宿諸生，謂之號房。

translations.literal: Beside the school quarters were built to lodge the students—these were called numbered lodgings.
translations.idiomatic: Dormitories beside the halls housed the students and were called numbered rooms.

sentences.zh: 厚給稟餼，歲時賜布帛文綺、襲衣巾靴。

translations.literal: They were generously supplied with grain stipends; at the seasons of the year they were granted cloth, silk brocade, full suits of clothing, caps, and boots.
translations.idiomatic: They received generous grain stipends and, at set seasons, gifts of cloth, brocade, full outfits, caps, and boots.

sentences.zh: 正旦元宵諸令節，俱賞節錢。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day, the Lantern Festival, and other statutory festivals, festival money was all granted.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day, the Lantern Festival, and other court holidays they received festival bonuses.

sentences.zh: 孝慈皇后積糧監中，置紅倉二十餘舍，養諸生之妻子。

translations.literal: Empress Xiaoci accumulated grain in the Directorate and established more than twenty Red Granary lodges to support the wives and children of the students.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiaoci stockpiled grain at the Directorate and set up more than twenty Red Granary storehouses to support students' families.

sentences.zh: 曆事生未娶者，賜錢婚聘，及女衣二襲，月米二石。

translations.literal: Service-training students who were not yet married were granted money for betrothal, two suits of women's clothing, and two shi of rice per month.
translations.idiomatic: Unmarried service-training students received betrothal funds, two sets of women's garments, and two shi of rice each month.

sentences.zh: 諸生在京師歲久，父母存，或父母亡而大父母、伯叔父母存，皆遣歸省，人賜衣一襲，鈔五錠，為道里費。

translations.literal: When students had been long in the capital, if parents were alive, or if parents were dead but grandparents or paternal uncles and aunts were alive, they were all sent home to pay respects; each was granted one suit of clothing and five ingots of paper money for travel expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Students who had been in the capital for years were sent home to visit parents, or—if parents had died—grandparents or uncles and aunts; each received a suit of clothes and five ingots of paper money for travel.

sentences.zh: 其優恤之如此。

translations.literal: Their generous care was to this extent.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the scale of their preferential treatment.

sentences.zh: 而其教之之法，每旦，祭酒、司業坐堂上，屬官自監丞以下，首領則典簿，以次序立。

translations.literal: As for the method of teaching them, each morning the libationer and vice-director sat in the hall above; subordinate officials from the directorate assistant down, with the registrar as head, stood in order.
translations.idiomatic: Each morning the libationer and vice-director presided in the main hall; subordinate officials down to the directorate assistants, led by the registrar, stood in ranked order.

sentences.zh: 諸生揖畢，質問經史，拱立聽命。

translations.literal: When the students had finished bowing, they questioned on the classics and histories, standing with hands joined to receive instructions.
translations.idiomatic: After bowing, students posed questions on the classics and histories, standing at attention to receive instruction.

sentences.zh: 惟朔望給假，餘日升堂會饌，乃會講、復講、背書，輪課以為常。

translations.literal: Only on the first and fifteenth of the month were holidays granted; on other days they ascended the hall for communal meals, then held joint lectures, review lectures, and recitation of texts—rotating lessons as the constant practice.
translations.idiomatic: They had leave only on the first and fifteenth of each month; on other days they dined together in hall, then held group lectures, review sessions, and recitations, with rotating assignments as the daily routine.

sentences.zh: 所習自《四子》本經外，兼及劉向說苑及律令、書、數、《御製大誥》。

translations.literal: What they studied, apart from the Four Books and their base classics, also included Liu Xiang's Shuoyuan, statutes and ordinances, writing, arithmetic, and the Imperially Composed Great Admonitions.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the Four Books and the canonical texts, the curriculum also covered Liu Xiang's Garden of Sayings, law codes, calligraphy, arithmetic, and the emperor's Great Admonitions.

sentences.zh: 每月試經、書義各一道，詔、誥、表、策論、判、內科二道。

translations.literal: Each month they were tested on one question each of classic meaning and book meaning, and two questions of edicts, mandates, memorials, policy essays, legal judgments, and inner-court subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Monthly examinations included one classic-interpretation and one literary-interpretation question, plus two questions in edicts, mandates, memorials, policy essays, legal judgments, and inner-court genres.

sentences.zh: 每日習書二百餘字，以二王、智永、歐、虞、顏、柳諸帖為法。

translations.literal: Each day they practiced more than two hundred characters in writing, taking as models the copybooks of the Two Wangs, Zhiyong, Ouyang, Yu, Yan, and Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Each day they copied more than two hundred characters, using master models from the Two Wangs, Zhiyong, and the Ouyang, Yu, Yan, and Liu traditions.

sentences.zh: 每班選一人充齋長，督諸生工課。

translations.literal: Each class selected one person to serve as dormitory head, supervising the students' daily work.
translations.idiomatic: Each class chose one dormitory head to oversee the students' daily assignments.

sentences.zh: 衣冠、步履、飲食，必嚴飭中節。

translations.literal: Dress, gait, food, and drink had all to be strictly regulated to proper measure.
translations.idiomatic: Dress, bearing, meals, and deportment were all strictly regulated.

sentences.zh: 夜必宿監，有故而出必告本班教官，令齋長帥之以白祭酒。

translations.literal: At night they had to lodge in the Directorate; if they had business to go out they had to inform their class instructor, and the dormitory head would lead them to report to the libationer.
translations.idiomatic: Students had to sleep in the Directorate; any departure required notice to the class instructor, and the dormitory head would report to the libationer.

sentences.zh: 監丞置集衍簿，有不遵者書之，再三犯者決責，四犯者至發遣安置。

translations.literal: The directorate assistant kept a cumulative misconduct register; those who did not comply were recorded; those who offended three times were beaten and punished; those who offended four times were even sent away for reassignment.
translations.idiomatic: The directorate assistant kept a misconduct register; offenders were recorded, thrice offenders were beaten, and four-time offenders could be expelled and reassigned.

sentences.zh: 其學規條目，屢次更定，寬嚴得其中。

translations.literal: The articles of study regulations were revised repeatedly, with leniency and severity balanced in the mean.
translations.idiomatic: Study regulations were revised several times until strictness and leniency struck a workable balance.

sentences.zh: 堂宇宿舍，飲饌澡浴，俱有禁例。

translations.literal: Halls, lodgings, food, drink, bathing, and washing all had prohibitory regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Rules governed every aspect of hall life, dormitories, meals, bathing, and washing.

sentences.zh: 省親、畢姻回籍，限期以道里遠近為差。

translations.literal: For returning home to visit parents or to complete marriage, deadlines were set according to the distance of the route.
translations.idiomatic: Leave to visit family or marry was granted for fixed periods scaled to travel distance.

sentences.zh: 違限者謫選遠方典史，有罰充吏者。

translations.literal: Those who exceeded the limit were demoted in selection to distant recorder posts; some were punished by assignment as clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Overstaying one's leave meant demotion to distant recorder posts, or in some cases assignment as clerks.

sentences.zh: 司教之官，必選耆宿。

translations.literal: Officials in charge of teaching had to be chosen from venerable elders.
translations.idiomatic: Teaching posts were reserved for senior scholars of established reputation.

sentences.zh: 宋訥、吳顒等由儒士擢祭酒，訥尤推名師。

translations.literal: Song Ne, Wu Yang, and others were promoted from Confucian scholars to libationer; Ne was especially acclaimed as a famous teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Song Ne, Wu Yang, and others rose from the scholarly ranks to libationer; Song Ne in particular was renowned as a master teacher.

sentences.zh: 曆科進士多出太學，而戊辰任亨泰廷對第一，太祖召訥褒賞，撰題名記，立石監門。

translations.literal: Jinshi of successive examination cycles mostly came from the Imperial Academy; in the wuchen year Ren Hengtai ranked first in the palace audience, and the Taizu summoned Ne to praise and reward him, composed a record of inscribed names, and set up a stone at the Directorate gate.
translations.idiomatic: Most jinshi came from the Imperial Academy; in the wuchen cycle (1388) Ren Hengtai topped the palace examination, and the founding emperor summoned Song Ne to honor him, composed an inscription record, and erected a stele at the Directorate gate.

sentences.zh: 辛未許觀亦如之。

translations.literal: In the xinwei year Xu Guan was treated the same way.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinwei cycle (1391) Xu Guan received the same honor.

sentences.zh: 進士題名碑由此相繼不絕。

translations.literal: From this the jinshi inscription steles continued in succession without break.
translations.idiomatic: Thus began the unbroken tradition of jinshi inscription stelae.

sentences.zh: 每歲天下按察司選生員年二十以上、厚重端秀者，送監考留。

translations.literal: Each year the surveillance commissions of the realm selected student members aged twenty or above who were solid and refined in bearing, and sent them to the Directorate for examination and retention.
translations.idiomatic: Each year provincial surveillance commissions chose student members over twenty who were mature and dignified and sent them to the Directorate for examination and enrollment.

sentences.zh: 會試下第舉人，入監卒業。

translations.literal: Provincial graduates who failed the metropolitan examination entered the Directorate to complete their studies.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial graduates who failed the metropolitan examination entered the Directorate to finish their training.

sentences.zh: 又因諫官關賢奏，設為定例。

translations.literal: It was also because the remonstrance official Guan Xian memorialized that this was established as a fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: After remonstrance official Guan Xian memorialized on the matter, the practice became a standing rule.

sentences.zh: 府、州、縣學歲貢生員各一人，翰林考試經、書義各一道，判語一條，中式者一等入國子監，二等達中都，不中者遣還，提調教官罰停廩祿。

translations.literal: Each prefectural, departmental, and county school presented one annual tribute student member; the Hanlin examined them on one question each of classic and book meaning and one legal judgment. Those who passed first class entered the Directorate of the Sons of the State, second class reached the Central Capital, and those who failed were sent back; the supervising instructors were fined by suspension of grain stipends.
translations.idiomatic: Each local school sent one annual tribute student; the Hanlin tested classic and literary interpretation plus one legal judgment. First-class passers entered the Imperial Directorate, second-class went to the Central Capital school, failures were sent home, and supervising teachers lost their stipends.

sentences.zh: 於是直省諸士子雲集輦下。

translations.literal: Thereupon scholars from the direct provinces gathered like clouds below the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars from the metropolitan provinces then flocked to the capital.

sentences.zh: 雲南、四川皆有士官生，日本、琉球、暹羅諸國亦皆有官生入監讀書，輒加厚賜，並給其從人。

translations.literal: Yunnan and Sichuan both had native-official students; Japan, Ryukyu, Siam, and other states also all had official students who entered the Directorate to study—they were always given generous additional rewards, and their attendants were also provided for.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan and Sichuan sent native-official students; Japan, Ryukyu, Siam, and other states sent official students to study at the Directorate, all receiving lavish gifts and support for their retinues.

sentences.zh: 永、宣間，先後絡繹。

translations.literal: Between the Yongle and Xuande reigns they came in succession without cease.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongle and Xuande reigns such delegations arrived in steady succession.

sentences.zh: 至成化、正德時，琉球生猶有至者。

translations.literal: By the Chenghua and Zhengde periods students from Ryukyu still came.
translations.idiomatic: As late as the Chenghua and Zhengde reigns Ryukyu students still arrived.

sentences.zh: 中都之置國學也，自洪武八年。

translations.literal: The establishment of the National Academy at the Central Capital dated from the eighth year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Capital National Academy was established in Hongwu 8 (1375).

sentences.zh: 至二十六年乃革，以其師生併入京師。

translations.literal: By the twenty-sixth year it was abolished, and its teachers and students were merged into the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 26 (1393) it was abolished and its faculty and students merged into the capital Directorate.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年始設北京國子監。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongle the Beijing Directorate of the Sons of the State was first established.
translations.idiomatic: Yongle 1 (1403) saw the founding of the Beijing Imperial Directorate.

sentences.zh: 十八年遷都，乃以京師國子監為南京國子監，而太學生有南北監之分矣。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the capital was moved; thereupon the capital Directorate of the Sons of the State became the Nanjing Directorate, and Imperial Academy students had a division between northern and southern Directorates.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital moved in Yongle 18 (1420), the former capital Directorate became Nanjing, and students were thereafter divided between northern and southern Directorates.

sentences.zh: 六堂諸生，有積分之法，司業二員分為左右，各提調三堂。

translations.literal: Students of the six halls had a method of accumulating points; the two vice-directors were divided into left and right, each supervising three halls.
translations.idiomatic: The six halls used a point-accumulation system; the two vice-directors split left and right, each overseeing three halls.

sentences.zh: 凡通《四書》未通經者，居正義、崇志、廣業。

translations.literal: All who had mastered the Four Books but not yet the classics resided in Upright Principle, Elevating Aspiration, and Broadening Work.
translations.idiomatic: Students who knew the Four Books but not yet the classics were placed in Upright Principle, Elevating Aspiration, and Broadening Work.

sentences.zh: 一年半以上，文理條暢者，升修道、誠心。

translations.literal: After more than a year and a half, those whose literary and classical learning flowed clearly were promoted to Cultivating the Way and Sincere Heart.
translations.idiomatic: After eighteen months, students whose literary and classical work was fluent advanced to Cultivating the Way and Sincere Heart.

sentences.zh: 又一年半，經史兼通、文理俱優者，乃升率性。

translations.literal: After another year and a half, those who mastered both classics and histories and were excellent in both literary and classical learning were then promoted to Following Nature.
translations.idiomatic: After another eighteen months, those who mastered classics and histories and excelled in both literary and classical studies rose to Following Nature.

sentences.zh: 升至率性，乃積分。

translations.literal: Only upon promotion to Following Nature did point accumulation begin.
translations.idiomatic: Point accumulation began only after promotion to Following Nature.

sentences.zh: 其法，孟月試本經義一道，仲月試論一道，詔、誥、表、內科一道，季月試經史第一道，判語二條。

translations.literal: The method was: in the first month of the season, test one question on the meaning of the base classic; in the middle month, one policy essay; in edicts, mandates, memorials, and inner-court subjects one question; in the last month, one question on classics and histories and two legal judgments.
translations.idiomatic: First month of each season: one base-classic question; second month: one policy essay; second month also: one edict, mandate, memorial, or inner-court question; third month: one classics-and-history question plus two legal judgments.

sentences.zh: 每試，文理俱優者與一分，理優文劣者與半分，紕繆者無分。

translations.literal: In each test, those excellent in both literary and classical learning received one point; those excellent in classical learning but weak in literary composition received half a point; those with errors received no points.
translations.idiomatic: Each examination awarded one point for excellence in both literary and classical work, half a point for strong classical but weak literary performance, and no points for flawed answers.

sentences.zh: 歲內積八分者為及格，與出身。

translations.literal: Those who accumulated eight points within the year were deemed to have passed and were granted qualification for office.
translations.idiomatic: Eight points within a year qualified a student for appointment.

sentences.zh: 不及者仍坐堂肄業。

translations.literal: Those who did not reach the standard still remained in the halls to continue study.
translations.idiomatic: Those who fell short remained in the halls to continue their studies.

sentences.zh: 如有才學超異者，奏請上裁。

translations.literal: If there were those of exceptionally surpassing talent and learning, a memorial was submitted requesting the emperor's decision.
translations.idiomatic: Exceptional students could be memorialized to the throne for special disposition.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十六年，盡擢監生劉政、龍鐔等六十四人為行省佈政、按察兩使，及參政、參議、副使、僉事等官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Hongwu, Directorate students Liu Zheng, Long Ting, and sixty-four others in all were entirely promoted to be provincial administration commissioners and surveillance commissioners of the branch secretariats, as well as participation commissioners, assistant commissioners, vice commissioners, and assistant surveillance commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 26 (1393) sixty-four Directorate students, including Liu Zheng and Long Ting, were promoted en masse to provincial administration and surveillance posts, along with various vice and assistant commissioner ranks.

sentences.zh: 其一旦而重用之，至於如此。

translations.literal: Their sudden heavy employment reached to this extent.
translations.idiomatic: The court could elevate them to such heights in a single stroke.

sentences.zh: 其為四方大吏者，蓋無算也。

translations.literal: Those who became great officials in the four directions were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Countless others became leading officials throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 李擴等自文華、武英擢御史，擴尋改給事中兼齊相府錄事，蓋臺諫之選亦出於太學。

translations.literal: Li Kuo and others were promoted from the Wenhua and Wuying halls to censor; Kuo was soon changed to supervising secretary concurrently with recorder of the Qi princely establishment—for censorial and remonstrance selections also came from the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kuo and others rose from the Wenhua and Wuying halls to censor, and Kuo soon became supervising secretary and recorder in the Qi princely household—showing that censorial and remonstrance posts also drew from the Academy.

sentences.zh: 其常調者乃為府、州、縣六品以下官。

translations.literal: Those of regular assignment became officials of the sixth rank and below in prefectures, departments, and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Routine appointments were to prefectural, departmental, and county posts of sixth rank and below.

sentences.zh: 初，以北方喪亂之餘，人鮮知學，遣國子生林伯雲等三百六十六人分教各郡。

translations.literal: At first, because after the chaos and ruin in the north few people knew learning, three hundred sixty-six Directorate students including Lin Boyun were dispatched to teach in the various commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, with learning scarce in the war-ravaged north, 366 Directorate students including Lin Boyun were sent to teach in the prefectures.

sentences.zh: 後乃推及他省，擇其壯歲能文者為教諭等官。

translations.literal: Later this was extended to other provinces, selecting those in their prime who could write to serve as instructors and similar offices.
translations.idiomatic: The program later spread to other provinces, appointing able writers in their prime as instructors and similar posts.

sentences.zh: 太祖雖間行科舉，而監生與薦舉人才參用者居多，故其時佈列中外者，太學生最盛。

translations.literal: Although the Taizu occasionally held examinations, Directorate students and recommended talent were mostly used together, so at that time those arrayed within and without, Imperial Academy students were most numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Though the founding emperor sometimes held civil examinations, Directorate students and recommended men still dominated appointments, and Academy graduates filled offices across the empire.

sentences.zh: 一再傳之後，進士日益重，薦舉遂廢，而舉貢日益輕。

translations.literal: After one or two generations, jinshi grew daily in weight, recommendation was then abandoned, and presented tribute scholars grew daily lighter.
translations.idiomatic: Within a generation or two jinshi status grew paramount, recommendation was abandoned, and tribute-presented scholars lost standing.

sentences.zh: 雖積分曆事不改初法，南北祭酒陳敬宗、李時勉等加意振飭，已漸不如其始。

translations.literal: Although the point system and service training did not change the original regulations, and the northern and southern libationers Chen Jingzong and Li Shimian gave special attention to revival and discipline, it already gradually fell short of the beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Point accumulation and service training remained on the books, and libationers Chen Jingzong and Li Shimian worked hard to restore standards, yet the Directorate steadily declined from its early vigor.

sentences.zh: 眾情所趨向，專在甲科。

translations.literal: The direction to which popular sentiment inclined was solely toward the top examination grade.
translations.idiomatic: Ambition focused exclusively on top examination honors.

sentences.zh: 宦途升沉，定於謁選之日。

translations.literal: Rise and fall on the official path were settled on the day of petitioning for selection.
translations.idiomatic: Career advancement or stagnation hinged on the day one petitioned for appointment.

sentences.zh: 監生不獲上第，即奮自鏃礪，不能有成，積重之勢然也。

translations.literal: Directorate students who did not obtain top rank, even if they strove to sharpen themselves, could not achieve success—such was the weight of accumulated tendency.
translations.idiomatic: Directorate students who failed to win top examination honors could strive all they liked yet rarely succeed—the weight of institutional habit made it so.

sentences.zh: 迨開納粟之例，則流品漸淆，且庶民亦得援生員之例以入監，謂之民生，亦謂之俊秀，而監生益輕。

translations.literal: When the regulation for contributing grain was opened, then ranks gradually became confused, and commoners could also invoke the student-member precedent to enter the Directorate—they were called common students, also called outstanding talents—and Directorate students grew still lighter.
translations.idiomatic: Once grain-purchase entry was allowed, status lines blurred; commoners could buy in as "common students" or "outstanding talents," and the Directorate student's standing sank further.

sentences.zh: 於是同處太學，而舉、貢得為府佐貳及州縣正官，官、恩生得選部、院、府、衛、司、寺小京職，尚為正途。

translations.literal: Thus though dwelling in the same Imperial Academy, examination and tribute students could become prefectural deputies and regular prefectural and county officials; official sons and grace sons could be selected for minor capital posts in ministries, courts, prefectures, guards, bureaus, and directorates—still counted as the proper route.
translations.idiomatic: Students in the same Academy faced unequal prospects: examination and tribute students could become prefectural deputies or county magistrates; official and grace sons could win minor capital posts in ministries and agencies—still the proper path.

sentences.zh: 而援例監生，僅得選州縣佐貳及府首領官；

translations.literal: But purchase-route Directorate students could only be selected for prefectural and county deputies and prefectural staff heads;
translations.idiomatic: Purchase-route Directorate students, by contrast, could only hope for county and prefectural deputy posts and prefectural staff headships;

sentences.zh: 其授京職者，乃光祿寺、上林苑之屬；

translations.literal: those granted capital offices were of the sort in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the Imperial Park;
translations.idiomatic: when they received capital posts, these were in agencies such as the Court of Imperial Sacrifices or the Imperial Park;

sentences.zh: 其願就遠方者，則以雲、貴、廣西及各邊省軍衛有司首領，及衛學、王府教授之缺用，而終身為異途矣。

translations.literal: those willing to go to distant regions were used to fill vacancies for staff heads in the military guards and civil offices of Yunnan, Guizhou, Guangxi, and the various border provinces, and for instructors in guard schools and princely establishments—and spent their lives on the irregular track.
translations.idiomatic: those willing to serve in the frontier took posts in Yunnan, Guizhou, Guangxi, border garrisons, guard schools, or princely academies—and spent their careers on the irregular track.

sentences.zh: 舉人入監，始於永樂中。

translations.literal: Provincial graduates entering the Directorate began in the Yongle period.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial graduates' enrollment in the Directorate began under Yongle.

sentences.zh: 會試下第，輒令翰林院錄其優者，俾入學以俟後科，給以教諭之俸。

translations.literal: Those who failed the metropolitan examination were promptly ordered by the Hanlin Academy to record the superior among them, so they might enter study to await the next examination cycle, and were given an instructor's salary.
translations.idiomatic: Metropolitan examination failures were screened by the Hanlin; the best were enrolled to await the next cycle and paid at instructor salary rates.

sentences.zh: 是時，會試有副榜，大抵署教官，故令入監者亦食其祿也。

translations.literal: At that time the metropolitan examination had a supplementary list; most were appointed instructors, so those ordered to enter the Directorate also received their salaries.
translations.idiomatic: The metropolitan examination then had a supplementary list, mostly appointing instructors—hence enrolled students received instructor pay.

sentences.zh: 宣德八年嘗命禮部尚書胡濙與大學士楊士奇、楊榮選副榜舉人龍文等二十四人，送監進學。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Xuande it was once ordered that Minister of Rites Hu Ying with Grand Secretaries Yang Shiqi and Yang Rong select twenty-four supplementary-list graduates such as Long Wen and send them to the Directorate for advanced study.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 8 (1433) Minister of Rites Hu Ying and Grand Secretaries Yang Shiqi and Yang Rong chose twenty-four supplementary-list graduates, including Long Wen, for advanced study at the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 翰林院三月一考其文，與庶起士同，頗示優異。

translations.literal: The Hanlin Academy examined their writings once every three months, the same as for shujiushi probationers, showing them considerable favor.
translations.idiomatic: The Hanlin tested their compositions every three months, on the same schedule as shujiushi probationers, a mark of special favor.

sentences.zh: 後不復另試，則取副榜年二十五以上者授教職，年未及者，或依親，或入監讀書。

translations.literal: Later separate examinations were no longer held; then supplementary-list graduates aged twenty-five or above were granted teaching offices, while those not yet of age either stayed with relatives or entered the Directorate to study.
translations.idiomatic: Separate examinations later ceased; supplementary-list men aged twenty-five or older received teaching posts, while younger ones either stayed with family or studied at the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 既而不拘年齒，依親、入監者皆聽。

translations.literal: Subsequently age was no longer restricted; both those staying with relatives and those entering the Directorate were all permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually age limits were dropped, and both family leave and Directorate study were allowed.

sentences.zh: 依親者，回籍讀書，依親肄業也。

translations.literal: Those staying with relatives returned to their native place to study—it was study while staying with relatives.
translations.idiomatic: Those on family leave returned home to study while living with relatives.

sentences.zh: 又有丁憂、成婚、省親、送幼子，皆仿依親例，限年復班。

translations.literal: There were also mourning for parents, marriage, visiting parents, and escorting young sons—all modeled on the precedent for staying with relatives, with a fixed term to return to class.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning leave, marriage leave, parental visits, and escorting young sons followed the same pattern, with fixed terms for returning to class.

sentences.zh: 正統中，天下教官多缺，而舉人厭其卑冷，多不願就。

translations.literal: In the Zhengtong period instructor posts throughout the realm were largely vacant, while provincial graduates disliked their low and cold status and mostly were unwilling to take them.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhengtong, instructor posts went unfilled nationwide because graduates shunned their low status and poor prospects.

sentences.zh: 十三年，御史萬節請敕禮部多取副榜，以就教職。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Censor Wan Jie requested an imperial order that the Ministry of Rites take more from the supplementary list to fill teaching offices.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 13 (1448) Censor Wan Jie asked the throne to order the Ministry of Rites to draw more supplementary-list graduates into teaching posts.

sentences.zh: 部臣以舉人願依親入監者十之七，願就教職者僅十之三，但宜各隨所欲，卻其請不行。

translations.literal: Ministry officials reported that seven-tenths of graduates wished to stay with relatives and enter the Directorate, while only three-tenths wished to take teaching offices; each should simply follow his own wish, and the request was rejected and not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry noted that seven in ten graduates preferred family leave or the Directorate, only three in ten wanted teaching posts, and rejected the proposal—each man should follow his preference.

sentences.zh: 至成化十三年，御史胡璘言：「天下教官率多歲貢，言行文章不足為人師範，請多取舉人選用，而罷貢生勿選。

translations.literal: By the thirteenth year of Chenghua, Censor Hu Lin said: "Instructors throughout the realm are mostly annual tribute scholars whose conduct, speech, and writings are insufficient to serve as models for others; I request that more provincial graduates be selected for use, and that tribute graduates cease to be selected."
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 13 (1477) Censor Hu Lin argued that most instructors were annual tribute scholars unfit to be moral exemplars, and urged appointing more provincial graduates while stopping tribute graduate appointments.

sentences.zh: 」部議歲貢如其舊，而舉人教官仍許會試。

translations.literal: " The ministry deliberated that annual tribute should remain as before, while graduate instructors were still permitted to take the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry kept annual tribute appointments unchanged but allowed graduate instructors to sit for the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 自後就教者亦漸多矣。

translations.literal: From then on those who took teaching offices also gradually increased.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter more graduates accepted teaching posts.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，南北國學皆空虛，議盡發下第舉人入監，且立限期以趣之。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing period both northern and southern National Academies were empty; it was proposed to send all failed metropolitan graduates into the Directorate and set deadlines to hurry them.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jiajing both Directorates stood nearly empty; officials proposed enrolling all failed metropolitan graduates and setting deadlines to compel attendance.

sentences.zh: 然舉人不願入監者，卒不可力強。

translations.literal: Yet those graduates unwilling to enter the Directorate ultimately could not be forced.
translations.idiomatic: Yet graduates who refused the Directorate could not be compelled.

sentences.zh: 於是生員歲貢之外，不得不頻舉選貢以充國學矣。

translations.literal: Thus beyond annual tribute from student members, selected tribute had to be held frequently to fill the National Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond annual tribute, the state had to hold frequent selected-tribute examinations to fill the Directorates.

sentences.zh: 貢生入監，初由生員選擇，既命各學歲貢一人，故謂之歲貢。

translations.literal: Tribute students entering the Directorate were at first chosen from student members; once each school was ordered to present one annually, they were therefore called annual tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute students originally came from local student selections; once each school was required to present one yearly, the practice was called annual tribute.

sentences.zh: 其例亦屢更。

translations.literal: Its regulations were also changed repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: The quotas were revised repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十一年，定府、州、縣學以一、二、三年為差。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Hongwu it was fixed that prefectural, departmental, and county schools should differ by one, two, and three years.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu 21 (1388) set prefectural, departmental, and county tribute cycles at one, two, and three years respectively.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，定府學歲二人，州學二歲三人，縣學歲一人。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year it was fixed: prefectural schools two per year, departmental schools three every two years, county schools one per year.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu 25 (1392) set quotas at two per year for prefectural schools, three every two years for departmental schools, and one per year for county schools.

sentences.zh: 永樂八年，定州縣戶不及五里者，州歲一人，縣間歲一人。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongle it was fixed that where departmental and county households did not reach five li, departments presented one per year and counties one every other year.
translations.idiomatic: Yongle 8 (1410) reduced quotas where populations were sparse: one per year for departments, one every other year for counties.

sentences.zh: 十九年，令歲貢照洪武二十一年例。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year annual tribute was ordered to follow the Hongwu twenty-first year precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Yongle 19 (1421) restored the Hongwu 21 quota system.

sentences.zh: 宣德七年，復照洪武二十五年例。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xuande it again followed the Hongwu twenty-fifth year precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Xuande 7 (1432) reverted to the Hongwu 25 quotas.

sentences.zh: 正統六年，更定府學歲一人，州學三歲二人，縣學間歲一人。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhengtong it was revised: prefectural schools one per year, departmental schools two every three years, county schools one every other year.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengtong 6 (1441) reset quotas to one per year for prefectures, two every three years for departments, and one every other year for counties.

sentences.zh: 弘治、嘉靖間，仍定府學歲二人，州學二歲三人，縣學歲一人，遂為永制。

translations.literal: Between Hongzhi and Jiajing it was again fixed at prefectural schools two per year, departmental schools three every two years, county schools one per year—thereafter becoming the permanent regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongzhi and Jiajing the Hongwu 25 quotas were restored as permanent law: two yearly for prefectures, three biennially for departments, one yearly for counties.

sentences.zh: 後孔、顏、孟三氏，及京學、衛學、都司、土官，川、雲、貴諸遠省，其按年充貢之法，亦間有增減云。

translations.literal: Later for the Kong, Yan, and Meng clans, capital schools, guard schools, regional commanders, native officials, and the distant provinces of Sichuan, Yunnan, and Guizhou, the methods of filling tribute quotas by year also had occasional increases and decreases.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius-family schools, capital and guard academies, native-official territories, and remote provinces such as Sichuan, Yunnan, and Guizhou had tribute quotas that were adjusted from time to time.

sentences.zh: 歲貢之始，必考學行端莊、文理優長者以充之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of annual tribute, conduct and learning, dignity, and excellence in literary and classical studies were always examined to fill the posts.
translations.idiomatic: Originally annual tribute required proven conduct, dignity, and strong literary and classical achievement.

sentences.zh: 其後但取食廩年深者。

translations.literal: Later only those long in receipt of grain stipends were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Later selection came down to whoever had held stipends the longest.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，南京祭酒章懋言：「洪、永間，國子生以數千計，今在監科貢共止六百餘人，歲貢挨次而升，衰遲不振者十常八九。

translations.literal: In the Hongzhi period Nanjing libationer Zhang Mao said: "Between Hongwu and Yongle, Directorate students numbered in the thousands; today examination, tribute, and purchase students in the Directorate total only six hundred-odd. Annual tribute advances by seniority in turn; nine or eight out of ten are decrepit, slow, and unvigorous."
translations.idiomatic: During Hongzhi, Nanjing libationer Zhang Mao wrote: "Under Hongwu and Yongle the Directorate held thousands of students; today barely six hundred remain. Annual tribute advances by seniority alone, and eight or nine in ten are elderly and feeble."

sentences.zh: 舉人坐監，又每後時。

translations.literal: Provincial graduates sitting in the Directorate also regularly arrived late.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial graduates enrolled in the Directorate habitually arrived late as well.

sentences.zh: 差撥不敷，教養罕效。

translations.literal: Assignments for service training were insufficient, and instruction and nurturing rarely took effect.
translations.idiomatic: Service assignments fell short, and training produced little result.

sentences.zh: 近年有增貢之舉，而所拔亦挨次之人，資格所拘，英才多滯。

translations.literal: In recent years there has been the measure of supplemental tribute, yet those selected are also persons advanced by turn; constrained by qualifications, many outstanding talents are held back.
translations.idiomatic: Recent supplemental tribute selections still favor seniority, so qualification rules block many able men.

sentences.zh: 乞於常貢外令提學行選貢之法，不分廩膳、增廣生員，通行考選，務求學行兼優、年富力強、累試優等者，乃以充貢。

translations.literal: I beg that beyond regular tribute the education intendant be ordered to conduct the method of selected tribute, without distinguishing stipend and augmented student members, conducting examinations universally, striving to find those excellent in both learning and conduct, vigorous in years and strength, and repeatedly testing in the top grade—only then to fill tribute posts.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that beyond regular tribute, education intendants hold competitive selected-tribute examinations open to all student members, choosing only men of proven learning and conduct, in their prime, with repeated top marks.

sentences.zh: 通計天下之廣，約取五六百人。

translations.literal: Estimating the breadth of the realm, take roughly five or six hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: Nationwide, select roughly five to six hundred men.

sentences.zh: 以後三、五年一行，則人才可漸及往年矣。

translations.literal: If this is conducted every three or five years thereafter, talent can gradually reach the level of former years.
translations.idiomatic: Held every three to five years, talent might again approach earlier levels.

sentences.zh: 」乃下部議行之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon it was sent down to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was referred to the ministries and adopted.

sentences.zh: 此選貢所由始也。

translations.literal: This was the origin of selected tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Thus began selected tribute.

sentences.zh: 選貢多英才，入監課試輒居上等，撥曆諸司亦有幹局。

translations.literal: Selected tribute scholars were mostly outstanding talents; entering the Directorate they regularly ranked at the top in lesson tests, and when assigned to serve in the various offices they also showed capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Selected tribute scholars were often gifted: in Directorate examinations they ranked at the top, and in office assignments they proved capable.

sentences.zh: 歲貢頹老，其勢日絀，則惟願就教而不願入監。

translations.literal: Annual tribute scholars were decrepit and aged; their momentum daily declined, so they only wished to take teaching offices and not to enter the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Annual tribute scholars grew old and weak, preferring teaching posts to the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十七年，祭酒程文德請將廷試歲貢惟留即選者於部，而其餘盡使入監。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Jiajing, libationer Cheng Wende requested that of annual tribute scholars in the palace examination only those immediately selected be kept at the ministry, while all the rest be made to enter the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 27 (1548) libationer Cheng Wende asked that only annual tribute men chosen at once in the palace examination remain at the ministry, sending all others to the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: The reply was approval.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 歲貢諸生合疏言，家貧親老，不願入監。

translations.literal: Annual tribute students jointly memorialized, saying their families were poor and parents aged, and they were unwilling to enter the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Annual tribute students petitioned collectively that poverty and aged parents kept them from the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 禮部復請從其所願，而盡使舉人入監。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites again requested to follow their wishes, while making all graduates enter the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites asked to honor their wishes while enrolling all graduates in the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 又從之。

translations.literal: This too was approved.
translations.idiomatic: This too was approved.

sentences.zh: 舉人入監不能如期，南京祭酒潘晟至請設重罰以趣其必赴。

translations.literal: Graduates entering the Directorate could not do so on schedule; Nanjing libationer Pan Sheng even requested heavy penalties to hurry them to attend without fail.
translations.idiomatic: Graduates failed to arrive on time; Nanjing libationer Pan Sheng proposed heavy penalties to force attendance.

sentences.zh: 於是舉人、選貢、歲貢三者迭為盛衰，而國學之盈虛亦靡有定也。

translations.literal: Thus graduates, selected tribute, and annual tribute alternated in rise and decline, and the fullness or emptiness of the National Academy also had no fixed pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Graduates, selected tribute, and annual tribute rose and fell in turn, and the Directorates' enrollment never held steady.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中，工科郭如心言：「選貢非祖制，其始欲補歲貢之乏，其後遂妨歲貢之途，請停其選。

translations.literal: In the Wanli period, Secretariat student Guo Ruxin said: "Selected tribute is not ancestral institution; at first it was meant to supplement the shortage of annual tribute, but later it obstructed the path of annual tribute; I request that the selection be stopped."
translations.idiomatic: During Wanli, Secretariat student Guo Ruxin argued that selected tribute was not ancestral law, had begun to fill gaps in annual tribute, but now blocked annual tribute's path, and asked that it be halted.

sentences.zh: 」神宗以為然。

translations.literal: " The Shenzong Emperor considered this correct.
translations.idiomatic: The Shenzong Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 至崇禎時，又嘗行之。

translations.literal: By the Chongzhen period it was again tried on occasion.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongzhen it was revived briefly.

sentences.zh: 恩貢者，國家有慶典或登極詔書，以當貢者充之。

translations.literal: Grace tribute scholars were appointed when the state had celebratory ceremonies or accession edicts, using those due for tribute to fill the posts.
translations.idiomatic: Grace tribute filled slots when the state celebrated great occasions or issued accession edicts, using students who would otherwise have been due for tribute.

sentences.zh: 而其次即為歲貢。

translations.literal: Those next in line then became annual tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The next candidates in line then became annual tribute scholars.

sentences.zh: 納貢視例監稍優，其實相仿也。

translations.literal: Purchased tribute was slightly superior to purchase-route Directorate students, but in reality they were much the same.
translations.idiomatic: Purchased tribute ranked slightly above purchase-route Directorate students, but in practice the two were much alike.

sentences.zh: 廕子入監，明初因前代任子之制，文官一品至七品，皆得廕一子以世其祿。

translations.literal: Yin sons entering the Directorate: at the beginning of Ming, following the former dynasty's system of appointing sons, civil officials from the first through seventh rank could all yin one son to inherit their salary.
translations.idiomatic: Yin sons entered the Directorate under early Ming rules inherited from earlier dynasties: civil officials of ranks one through seven could nominate one son to inherit their stipend.

sentences.zh: 後乃漸為限制，在京三品以上方得請廕，謂之官生。

translations.literal: Later this was gradually restricted: only those of the third rank and above in the capital could request yin—these were called official sons.
translations.idiomatic: Restrictions tightened until only capital officials of third rank or higher could secure yin—these were called official sons.

sentences.zh: 出自特恩者，不限官品，謂之恩生。

translations.literal: Those arising from special grace were not limited by rank and were called grace sons.
translations.idiomatic: Special imperial grace, without rank limits, produced grace sons.

sentences.zh: 或即與職事，或送監讀書。

translations.literal: Some were immediately given official duties, others were sent to the Directorate to study.
translations.idiomatic: Some received offices immediately; others were sent to study at the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 官生必三品京官，成化三年從助教李伸言也。

translations.literal: Official sons required third-rank capital officials—this followed teaching assistant Li Shen's proposal in the third year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: The third-rank capital requirement for official sons followed teaching assistant Li Shen's proposal in Chenghua 3 (1467).

sentences.zh: 時給事中李森不可。

translations.literal: At the time supervising secretary Li Sen disapproved.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Li Sen objected.

sentences.zh: 帝諭，責其刻薄；

translations.literal: The emperor instructed, rebuking him for harshness;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked him for harshness;

sentences.zh: 第令非歷任年久政績顯著者，毋得濫敘而已。

translations.literal: only ordering that those without long service and outstanding achievements in office must not be recklessly enrolled.
translations.idiomatic: only requiring that yin not be granted without long service and distinguished achievement.

sentences.zh: 既得廕敘，由提學官考送部試，如貢生例，送入監中。

translations.literal: Once yin enrollment was obtained, they were examined and sent by the education intendant to the ministry for testing, as with tribute students, and entered the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: After yin enrollment, education intendants examined them and sent them for ministry tests, as with tribute students, then into the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 時內閣呂原子翾由廕監補中書舍人，七年辛卯乞應順天鄉試。

translations.literal: At the time Lü Yuan's son Lü Xuan of the Grand Secretariat, having been supplemented as a Secretariat drafter from yin Directorate status, in the seventh year xinmao begged to take the Shuntian provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Lü Yuan's son Lü Xuan, appointed Secretariat drafter through yin status, in Chenghua 7 (1471) asked to sit for the Shuntian provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 部請從之。

translations.literal: The ministry requested approval.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry approved the request.

sentences.zh: 給事中芮畿不可。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Rui Ji disapproved.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Rui Ji objected.

sentences.zh: 帝允翾所請，不為例。

translations.literal: The emperor granted Xuan's request, not making it a precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted Xuan's request as an exception, not a precedent.

sentences.zh: 然其後以廕授舍人者，俱得應舉矣。

translations.literal: Yet afterward those granted drafter posts through yin were all permitted to take examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Later, yin appointees to drafter posts were all allowed to take examinations.

sentences.zh: 嘉、隆以後，宰相之子有初授即為尚寶司丞，徑轉本司少卿，由光祿、太常以躋九列者，又有以軍功廕錦衣者，往往不由太學。

translations.literal: After Jiajing and Longqing, chancellors' sons were some appointed at first as vice commissioners of the Imperial Seals Office, transferred directly to junior director of that office, or advanced through the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the Court of the Imperial Clan to the nine ranks; there were also those yinned into the Embroidered Uniform Guard through military merit—often not passing through the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiajing and Longqing, prime ministers' sons might enter as vice commissioners of the Imperial Seals Office and rise straight to director, or climb through ritual agencies to ministerial rank; military yin into the Embroidered Uniform Guard often bypassed the Academy entirely.

sentences.zh: 其他併入監。

translations.literal: All others were merged into the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Others still entered the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 恩生之始，建文元年錄吳雲子黼為國子生，以雲死節雲南也。

translations.literal: The beginning of grace sons: in the first year of Jianwen, Wu Yun's son Wu Fu was enrolled as a Directorate student because Yun died maintaining integrity in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Grace sons began in Jianwen 1 (1399), when Wu Yun's son Wu Fu was enrolled because Yun had died defending Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 正德十六年定例，凡文武官死於忠諫者，一子入監。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Zhengde a fixed regulation was made: for all civil and military officials who died in loyal remonstrance, one son entered the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 16 (1521) fixed the rule that one son of any official who died in loyal remonstrance entered the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 其後守土官死節亦皆得廕子矣。

translations.literal: Later territorial officials who died maintaining integrity also all obtained yin for their sons.
translations.idiomatic: Later, local officials who died defending their posts also won yin for their sons.

sentences.zh: 又弘治十八年定例，東宮侍從官，講讀年久輔導有功者，歿後，子孫乞恩，禮部奏請上裁。

translations.literal: Also in the eighteenth year of Hongzhi a fixed regulation was made: for Eastern Palace attendants who lectured and read the classics for many years with meritorious guidance, after death their descendants might beg grace; the Ministry of Rites memorialized requesting the emperor's decision.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 18 (1505) also ruled that after the death of long-serving Eastern Palace tutors, descendants could petition for grace through the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 正德元年復定，其祖父年勞已及三年者，一子即授試中書舍人習字；

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengde it was again fixed: where the grandfather's years of service had reached three, one son was immediately granted probationary Secretariat drafter to practice writing;
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 1 (1506) restored the rule that if a grandfather had served three years, one grandson received probationary drafter status at once;

sentences.zh: 未及三年者，一子送監讀書。

translations.literal: those not yet reaching three years, one son was sent to the Directorate to study.
translations.idiomatic: if service fell short of three years, one son was sent to the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 八年復定，東宮侍班官三年者，一子入監。

translations.literal: In the eighth year it was again fixed: Eastern Palace attendance officers of three years, one son entered the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 8 (1513) ruled that three years' service as Eastern Palace attendants entitled one son to the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 又萬曆十二年定例，三品日講官，雖未考滿，一子入監。

translations.literal: Also in the twelfth year of Wanli a fixed regulation was made: third-rank daily lecture officials, even if their evaluation term was not complete, one son entered the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 12 (1584) granted one son of a third-rank daily lecturer entry to the Directorate even before the term of service ended.

sentences.zh: 例監始於景泰元年，以邊事孔棘，令天下納粟納馬者入監讀書，限千人止。

translations.literal: Purchase-route Directorate students began in the first year of Jingtai; because border affairs were critically urgent, those throughout the realm who contributed grain or horses were ordered to enter the Directorate to study, limited to one thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: Purchase-route students began in Jingtai 1 (1450), when border crises led the state to admit men who contributed grain or horses, capped at one thousand.

sentences.zh: 行四年而罷。

translations.literal: It was carried out for four years and then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The policy ran four years, then ended.

sentences.zh: 成化二年，南京大饑，守臣建議，欲令官員軍民子孫納粟送監。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chenghua there was great famine in Nanjing; defending officials proposed that sons and grandsons of officials, soldiers, and commoners contribute grain to be sent to the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 2 (1466), during severe famine in Nanjing, local officials proposed admitting sons of officials, soldiers, and commoners who contributed grain.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書姚夔言：「太學乃育才之地，近者直省起送四十歲生員，及納草納馬者動以萬計，不勝其濫。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Yao Kui said: "The Imperial Academy is a place for nurturing talent; recently the direct provinces have sent up forty-year-old student members, and those contributing fodder or horses number in the tens of thousands—the excess cannot be borne."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Yao Kui objected: "The Academy exists to cultivate talent, yet provinces now send forty-year-old students, and grain and horse purchasers number in the tens of thousands—the abuse is unbearable."

sentences.zh: 且使天下以貨為賢，士風日陋。

translations.literal: Moreover it makes the realm take wealth as worthiness, and scholarly custom grows daily coarse.
translations.idiomatic: It teaches the empire to value wealth over merit, debasing scholarly culture day by day.

sentences.zh: 」帝以為然，為卻守臣之議。

translations.literal: " The emperor considered this correct and rejected the defending officials' proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and rejected the local officials' plan.

sentences.zh: 然其後或遇歲荒，或因邊警，或大興工作，率援往例行之，訖不能止。

translations.literal: Yet afterward whenever there was famine, or border alarms, or great construction works, precedent was always invoked to carry it out, and in the end it could not be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yet famine, border crises, or major construction repeatedly revived the practice by precedent, and it never ceased entirely.

sentences.zh: 此舉、貢、廕、例諸色監生，前後始末之大凡也。

translations.literal: This is the broad outline of the origins and outcomes, first and last, of the various kinds of Directorate students—examination, tribute, yin, and purchase.
translations.idiomatic: Such, in broad outline, is the history of examination, tribute, yin, and purchase-route Directorate students.

sentences.zh: 監生曆事，始於洪武五年。

translations.literal: Directorate students' service training began in the fifth year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Service training for Directorate students began in Hongwu 5 (1372).

sentences.zh: 建文時，定考覈法上、中、下三等。

translations.literal: In the Jianwen period an evaluation method was fixed with upper, middle, and lower three grades.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jianwen, evaluations were divided into upper, middle, and lower grades.

sentences.zh: 上等選用，中、下等仍曆一年再考。

translations.literal: The upper grade was selected for appointment; middle and lower grades continued service for one year and were examined again.
translations.idiomatic: Upper-grade students received appointments; middle and lower grades served another year and were re-examined.

sentences.zh: 上等者依上等用，中等者不拘品級，隨才任用，下等者回監讀書。

translations.literal: Upper-grade students were used according to the upper grade; middle-grade students were not bound by rank but appointed according to talent; lower-grade students returned to the Directorate to study.
translations.idiomatic: Upper-grade men were appointed accordingly; middle-grade men were placed without rank restrictions according to ability; lower-grade men returned to study.

sentences.zh: 永樂五年，選監生三十八人隸翰林院，習四夷譯書。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongle thirty-eight Directorate students were selected to serve under the Hanlin Academy and study translation of the four barbarian languages.
translations.idiomatic: Yongle 5 (1407) assigned thirty-eight Directorate students to the Hanlin to study foreign-language translation.

sentences.zh: 九年辛卯，鐘英等五人成進士，俱改庶起士。

translations.literal: In the ninth year xinmao, five men including Zhong Ying became jinshi and were all changed to shujiushi probationers.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 9 (1411) five men including Zhong Ying passed as jinshi and became Hanlin shujiushi probationers.

sentences.zh: 壬辰、乙未以後，譯書中會試者甚多，皆改庶起士，以為常。

translations.literal: After renchen and yiwei, many among the translators passed the metropolitan examination; all were changed to shujiushi probationers, and this became customary.
translations.idiomatic: After 1412 and 1415 many translators passed the metropolitan examination and routinely became shujiushi probationers.

sentences.zh: 曆事生成名，其蒙恩遇如此。

translations.literal: Service-training students achieved fame; the favor they received was to this extent.
translations.idiomatic: Service trainees could rise to such renown and imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 仁宗初政，中軍都督府奏監生七人吏事勤慎，請注選授官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Renzong Emperor's rule, the Central Military Commission memorialized that seven Directorate students were diligent and careful in administrative affairs and requested registered selection for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Renzong's reign the Central Military Commission asked to appoint seven diligent service trainees.

sentences.zh: 帝不許，仍令入學，由科舉以進。

translations.literal: The emperor did not permit it and still ordered them to enter study, advancing through the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused and ordered them back to study, to advance through the examinations.

sentences.zh: 他曆事者，多不願還監。

translations.literal: Other service trainees mostly were unwilling to return to the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Most other service trainees likewise refused to return.

sentences.zh: 於是通政司引奏，六科辦事監生二十人滿日，例應還監，仍願就科辦事。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Communications Office presented a memorial: twenty Directorate students serving in the Six Sections had completed their term and by regulation should return to the Directorate, yet still wished to continue service in the Sections.
translations.idiomatic: The Communications Office reported that twenty Six-Section trainees had finished their term and should return to the Directorate, yet wished to remain in section service.

sentences.zh: 帝復召二十人者，諭令進學。

translations.literal: The emperor again summoned the twenty men and instructed them to advance in study.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned all twenty and ordered them back to their studies.

sentences.zh: 蓋是時，六科給事中多缺，諸生覬得之。

translations.literal: For at that time the Six Sections' supervising secretaries were largely vacant, and the students coveted those posts.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many supervising secretary posts in the Six Sections stood vacant, and students coveted them.

sentences.zh: 帝察知其意，故不授官也。

translations.literal: The emperor perceived their intent and therefore did not grant office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw their ambition and withheld appointments.

sentences.zh: 宣宗以教官多缺，選用監生三百八十人，而程富等以都御史顧佐之薦，使於各道曆政三月，選擇任之，所謂試御史也。

translations.literal: The Xuande Emperor, because instructor posts were largely vacant, selected three hundred eighty Directorate students for use; Cheng Fu and others, on the recommendation of censor-in-chief Gu Zuo, were sent to practice administration in the various circuits for three months, then selected and appointed—the so-called probationary censors.
translations.idiomatic: Xuande filled vacant instructor posts with 380 Directorate students; Cheng Fu and others, recommended by Censor-in-Chief Gu Zuo, served three-month administrative apprenticeships in the circuits—the probationary censors.

sentences.zh: 監生撥曆，初以入監年月為先後，丁憂、省祭，有在家延留七八年者，比至入監，即得取撥。

translations.literal: Assignment for service training at first took entry year and month as the order of precedence; for mourning or sacrificial leave some remained at home seven or eight years, and by the time they entered the Directorate they could immediately receive assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Assignments initially followed enrollment date, but men who spent seven or eight years at home for mourning or sacrifices could enter and receive assignment at once.

sentences.zh: 陳敬宗、李時勉先後題請，一以坐監年月為淺深。

translations.literal: Chen Jingzong and Li Shimian successively submitted requests that precedence be determined solely by the year and month of residence in the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingzong and Li Shimian petitioned that precedence depend solely on time actually spent in the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 其後又以存省、京儲、依親、就學、在家年月，亦作坐堂之數。

translations.literal: Later years spent on parental visits, capital grain storage duty, staying with relatives, pursuing study, and time at home were also counted as time in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Later, time on parental leave, capital grain service, family leave, outside study, or at home also counted toward hall residence.

sentences.zh: 其患病及他事故，始以虛曠論。

translations.literal: Only illness and other incidents were treated as empty absence.
translations.idiomatic: Only illness and similar emergencies counted as unauthorized absence.

sentences.zh: 諸生互爭年月資次，各援科條。

translations.literal: Students disputed one another over years, months, and seniority, each citing regulatory articles.
translations.idiomatic: Students quarreled over seniority by year and month, each citing regulations in support.

sentences.zh: 成化五年，祭酒陳鑒以兩詞具聞，乞敕禮部酌中定制，為禮科所駁。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chenghua, libationer Chen Jian reported both versions in full, begging an imperial order that the Ministry of Rites deliberate a moderate fixed regulation; this was rejected by the Rites Section.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 5 (1469) libationer Chen Jian memorialized both sides and asked the Ministry of Rites to set a balanced rule; the Rites Section rejected it.

sentences.zh: 鑒復奏，互爭之。

translations.literal: Jian memorialized again, and they disputed each other.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jian memorialized again, and the dispute continued.

sentences.zh: 乃下部覆議，請一一精核，仍計地理遠近、水程日月以為準。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was sent to the ministries for review, requesting meticulous verification case by case, still calculating distance of geography, water routes, and days and months as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: The case went to the ministries for review, calling for case-by-case verification using distance, travel routes, and elapsed time as standards.

sentences.zh: 然文稱往來，紛錯繁揉，上下伸縮，弊端甚多，卒不能畫一也。

translations.literal: Yet documents went back and forth, tangled and confused, stretched and contracted above and below; abuses were many, and in the end uniformity could not be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials flew back and forth in confusion, rules stretched and contracted, abuses multiplied, and uniformity never prevailed.

sentences.zh: 初令監生由廣業升率性，始得積分出身。

translations.literal: At first Directorate students were ordered to rise from Broadening Work to Following Nature before they could accumulate points for qualification.
translations.idiomatic: Originally students had to advance from Broadening Work to Following Nature before point accumulation qualified them for office.

sentences.zh: 天順以前，在監十餘年，然後撥曆諸司，曆事三月，仍留一年，送吏部銓選。

translations.literal: Before Tianshun, one remained in the Directorate more than ten years, then was assigned to serve in the various offices; after three months of service one still remained one year, then was sent to the Ministry of Personnel for evaluation and selection.
translations.idiomatic: Before Tianshun, students spent ten-plus years in the Directorate, then three months in office service plus another year before Ministry of Personnel selection.

sentences.zh: 其兵部清黃及隨御史出巡者，則以三年為率。

translations.literal: Those doing Ministry of War Qinghuang roster work and accompanying censors on inspection tours took three years as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry of War roster compilation and censor inspection tours, by contrast, used a three-year standard.

sentences.zh: 其後，以監生積滯者多，頻減撥曆歲月以疏通之。

translations.literal: Afterwards, because many Directorate students had accumulated delays, the months for office assignments were repeatedly reduced to clear the blockage.
translations.idiomatic: Later, with many students backed up in the Directorate, office-service terms were repeatedly shortened to relieve the backlog.

sentences.zh: 每歲揀選，優者輒與撥曆，有未及一年者。

translations.literal: Each year in selection, superior ones were immediately given office assignments; some had not yet reached one year.
translations.idiomatic: In annual selection the best were assigned to offices at once, sometimes before a full year in the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 弘治八年，監生在監者少，而吏部聽選至萬餘人，有十餘年不得官者。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Hongzhi, few students remained in the Directorate, while those awaiting Ministry of Personnel selection reached more than ten thousand; some had gone more than ten years without office.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 8 (1495) fewer than usual students sat in the Directorate while over ten thousand awaited Ministry of Personnel selection, some for more than a decade.

sentences.zh: 祭酒林瀚以坐班人少，不敷撥曆，請開科貢。

translations.literal: Libationer Lin Han, because sitting-shift students were too few to fill office assignments, requested opening examination-recruitment quotas.
translations.idiomatic: Libationer Lin Han, finding too few students on sitting shifts to fill office quotas, asked to expand examination and tribute recruitment.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書倪嶽覆奏，科舉已有定額，不可再增，惟請增歲貢人數，而定諸司曆事，必須日月滿後，方與更替，使諸生坐監稍久，選人亦無壅滯。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Ni Yue memorialized in reply: metropolitan examination already had fixed quotas and could not be increased further; he only requested increasing annual tribute numbers, and fixing that office service in the ministries must complete the full days and months before replacement, so students would sit in the Directorate somewhat longer and those awaiting selection would not stagnate.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Ni Yue replied that examination quotas were fixed, but asked to raise annual tribute intake and require full completion of ministry service before rotation, keeping students in the Directorate longer and easing the selection backlog.

sentences.zh: 及至嘉靖十年，監生在監者不及四百人，諸司曆事歲額以千計。

translations.literal: By the tenth year of Jiajing, fewer than four hundred students remained in the Directorate, while annual office-service quotas across ministries numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: By Jiajing 10 (1531) fewer than four hundred students remained in the Directorate while ministry service quotas ran to thousands per year.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書李時引嶽前議言：「嶽權宜二法，一增歲額以足坐班生徒，一議差曆以久坐班歲月。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Li Shi cited Ni Yue's earlier proposal, saying: "Ni Yue proposed two expedient measures—one to increase annual quotas to fill sitting-shift students, one to adjust service assignments to prolong sitting-shift months."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Li Shi cited Ni Yue's earlier plan: two expedients—raise annual quotas to fill sitting shifts, and adjust service terms to keep students in the Directorate longer.

sentences.zh: 於是府、州、縣學以一歲二貢、二歲三貢、一歲一貢為差，行之四歲而止。

translations.literal: Thereupon prefectural, departmental, and county schools were differentiated as two tributes in one year, three tributes in two years, and one tribute in one year; this was carried out for four years then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural, departmental, and county schools were then graded at two tributes per year, three per two years, and one per year; the scheme ran four years and ended.

sentences.zh: 其諸司曆事，三月考勤之後，仍曆一年，其餘寫本一年，清黃、寫誥、清軍、清匠三年，以至出巡等項，俱如舊例日月。

translations.literal: For office service in the ministries, after three months of attendance review one still served one year; copying records one year; Qinghuang, drafting edicts, military roster review, and artisan roster review three years; and inspection tours and similar items all followed the old terms in days and months.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry service after three months' attendance review still lasted one year; record copying one year; roster work, edict drafting, military and artisan reviews three years; inspection tours and the like kept their former terms.

sentences.zh: 今國學缺人，視弘治間更甚，請將前件事例，參酌舉行。

translations.literal: Now the Imperial Academy lacks people even more than in the Hongzhi period; please consider and implement the previous precedents.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Academy now faces a worse shortage than in the Hongzhi era; please weigh and enact the earlier precedents.

sentences.zh: 」並從之，獨不增貢額。

translations.literal: All was approved except increasing tribute quotas.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved all of this except the increase in tribute quotas.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復以祭酒許誥、提學御史胡時善之請，詔增貢額，如嶽、時前議。
