translations.literal: Before long, at the request of libationer Xu Gao and education inspector Hu Shishan, an edict increased tribute quotas as Ni Yue and Li Shi had previously proposed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, at the request of libationer Xu Gao and education inspector Hu Shishan, an edict raised tribute quotas along the lines Ni Yue and Li Shi had urged.

sentences.zh: 隆、萬以後，學校積馳，一切循故事而已。

translations.literal: After Longqing and Wanli, schools gradually declined; everything simply followed precedent.
translations.idiomatic: After the Longqing and Wanli reigns schools slid into neglect, and policy amounted to going through the motions.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年，從司業倪嘉善言，復行積分法。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongzhen, following vice-director Ni Jiashan's proposal, the point-accumulation system was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 2 (1629), on vice-director Ni Jiashan's advice, the point-accumulation system was revived.

sentences.zh: 八年，從祭酒倪元璐言，以貢選為正流，援納為閏流。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, following libationer Ni Yuanlu's proposal, tribute selection became the regular stream and purchase-entry the intercalary stream.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 8 (1635) libationer Ni Yuanlu had tribute selection treated as the regular stream and purchase-entry as the intercalary stream.

sentences.zh: 貢選不限撥期，以積分歲滿為率，援納則依原定撥曆為率。

translations.literal: Tribute selection was not limited by assignment periods; completion of accumulated years was the standard; purchase-entry followed the originally fixed office-assignment schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute students faced no fixed assignment deadline but qualified when accumulated years were complete; purchase-entry students kept the original office-service schedule.

sentences.zh: 而曆事不分正雜，惟以考定等第為曆期多寡。

translations.literal: Office service no longer distinguished regular from miscellaneous assignment; only examination grade determined the length of service.
translations.idiomatic: Service assignments no longer split regular and miscellaneous posts; term length depended solely on examination grade.

sentences.zh: 諸司教之政事，勿與猥雜差遣。

translations.literal: The ministries were to teach administrative affairs and not assign vulgar miscellaneous duties.
translations.idiomatic: Ministries were to train students in administration and keep them from petty errands.

sentences.zh: 滿日，校其勤惰，開報吏部。

translations.literal: When the term ended, diligence and laziness were assessed and reported to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: At term's end diligence was graded and reported to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 不率者，回監教習。

translations.literal: Those who did not comply returned to the Directorate for further instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Noncompliant students were sent back to the Directorate for retraining.

sentences.zh: 時監規頹廢已久，不能振作也。

translations.literal: By then Directorate regulations had long been in decline and could not be revived.
translations.idiomatic: Directorate rules had by then decayed too long to be restored.

sentences.zh: 凡監生曆事，吏部四十一名，戶部五十三名，禮部十三名，大理寺二十八名，通政司五名，行人司四名，五軍都督府五十名，謂之正曆。

translations.literal: For Directorate students' office service: the Ministry of Personnel forty-one, Ministry of Revenue fifty-three, Ministry of Rites thirteen, Court of Judicial Review twenty-eight, Office of Transmission five, Court of State Ceremonial four, Five Military Commissions fifty—called regular service.
translations.idiomatic: Regular service quotas were forty-one at the Ministry of Personnel, fifty-three at Revenue, thirteen at Rites, twenty-eight at the Court of Judicial Review, five at Transmission, four at State Ceremonial, and fifty at the Five Military Commissions.

sentences.zh: 三月上選，滿日增減不定。

translations.literal: Selection came in the third month; increases and decreases upon completion of the term were not fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Selection occurred in the third month, with no fixed rule for adjusting quotas when terms ended.

sentences.zh: 又有諸司寫本，戶部十名，禮部十八名，兵部二十名，刑部十四名，工部八名，都察院十四名，大理寺、通政司俱四名，隨御史出巡四十二名，謂之雜曆。

translations.literal: There were also copying assignments in the ministries: Ministry of Revenue ten, Ministry of Rites eighteen, Ministry of War twenty, Ministry of Justice fourteen, Ministry of Works eight, Censorate fourteen, Court of Judicial Review and Office of Transmission four each, accompanying censors on inspection forty-two—called miscellaneous service.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous service meant copying posts: ten at Revenue, eighteen at Rites, twenty at War, fourteen at Justice, eight at Works, fourteen at the Censorate, four each at Judicial Review and Transmission, and forty-two with touring censors.

sentences.zh: 一年滿日上選。

translations.literal: Upon completion of one year, selection was submitted.
translations.idiomatic: After one year nominations went upward for selection.

sentences.zh: 又有諸色辦事，清黃一百名，寫誥四十名，續黃五十名，清軍四十名，天財庫十名，初以三年謂之長差，後改一年上選；

translations.literal: There were also various clerical assignments: Qinghuang one hundred, drafting edicts forty, supplementary roster fifty, military roster review forty, Celestial Wealth Storehouse ten—initially three-year long assignments, later changed to one-year upward selection;
translations.idiomatic: Other clerical posts included one hundred for Qinghuang, forty for edict drafting, fifty for supplementary rosters, forty for military reviews, and ten at the Celestial Wealth Storehouse—first three-year long assignments, later one-year terms with upward selection;

sentences.zh: 承運庫十五名，司禮監十六名，尚寶司六名，六科四十名，初作短差，後亦定一年上選。

translations.literal: Receiving-Fortune Storehouse fifteen, Directorate of Ceremonial sixteen, Imperial Credentials Office six, Six Offices forty—initially short assignments, later also fixed at one year for upward selection.
translations.idiomatic: the Receiving-Fortune Storehouse fifteen, Directorate of Ceremonial sixteen, Imperial Credentials Office six, and Six Offices forty—short assignments at first, later also one-year terms with upward selection.

sentences.zh: 又有隨御史刷卷一百七十八名，工部清匠六十名，俱事完日上選。

translations.literal: There were also one hundred seventy-eight accompanying censors reviewing files and sixty artisan roster reviews in the Ministry of Works; all submitted for selection upon completion of the task.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred seventy-eight censorial file reviewers and sixty Works artisan-roster posts also went up for selection when duties ended.

sentences.zh: 又有禮部寫民情條例七十二名，光祿寺刷卷四名，修齋八名，參表二十名，報訃二十名，齎俸十二名，錦衣衛四名，兵部查馬冊三十名，工部大木廠二十名，後府磨算十名，御馬監四名，天財庫四名，正陽門四名，崇文、宣武、朝陽、東直俱三名，阜城、西直、安定、德勝俱二名，以半年滿日回監。

translations.literal: There were also seventy-two copying popular regulations in the Ministry of Rites, four file reviewers in the Court of Imperial Entertainments, eight fasting ritual posts, twenty memorial presenters, twenty death-notice couriers, twelve salary bearers, four in the Embroidered Uniform Guard, thirty horse-register checks in the Ministry of War, twenty at the Great Timber Yard in the Ministry of Works, ten calculation clerks in the Rear Palace Office, four in the Imperial Horse Directorate, four in the Celestial Wealth Storehouse, four at Zhengyang Gate, three each at Chongwen, Xuanwu, Chaoyang, and Dongzhi gates, two each at Fucheng, Xizhi, Anding, and Desheng gates—returning to the Directorate upon half a year's completion.
translations.idiomatic: Shorter posts included seventy-two Ministry of Rites clerks copying popular regulations, plus file review, fasting ritual, memorial, death-notice, and salary courier slots at Entertainments, Guard, War, Works, palace offices, and city gates—students returned after six months.

sentences.zh: 郡縣之學，與太學相維，創立自唐始。

translations.literal: Prefectural and county schools, interlinked with the Imperial Academy, were first established in the Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural and county schools, paired with the Imperial Academy, date from the Tang.

sentences.zh: 宋置諸路州學官，元頗因之，其法皆未具。

translations.literal: The Song established circuit and prefectural school officials; the Yuan largely followed this, but the regulations were not complete.
translations.idiomatic: Song created circuit and prefectural school officers; Yuan largely kept them, though the rules were never fully spelled out.

sentences.zh: 迄期，天下府、州、縣、衛所，皆建儒學，教官四千二百餘員，弟子無算，教養之法備矣。

translations.literal: By that time, Confucian schools had been built in every prefecture, department, county, and guard post throughout the realm; instructors numbered more than four thousand two hundred, students were beyond counting, and methods of instruction and nurture were complete.
translations.idiomatic: By the founding of the dynasty every prefecture, department, county, and guard post had a Confucian school, with more than 4,200 instructors and countless students; instruction was fully in place.

sentences.zh: 洪武二年，太祖初建國學，諭中書省臣曰：「學校之教，至元其弊極矣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Hongwu, when the Taizu first established the Imperial Academy, he instructed the Secretariat officials, saying: "School education under the Yuan reached its worst abuses."
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 2 (1369), as the Hongwu Emperor first built the Imperial Academy, he told Secretariat officials: "Schools under the Yuan had sunk to their lowest point."

sentences.zh: 上下之間，波頹風靡，學校雖設，名存實亡。

translations.literal: Between high and low, waves crashed and winds blew; though schools were set up, names existed but reality was gone.
translations.idiomatic: From court to countryside standards collapsed; schools existed in name only.

sentences.zh: 兵變以來，人習戰爭，惟知干戈，莫識俎豆。

translations.literal: Since the military upheavals, people had grown used to war and knew only arms, no longer recognizing ritual vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Years of war had taught men the sword but not the rites.

sentences.zh: 朕惟治國以教化為先，教化以學校為本。

translations.literal: I consider that governing the state takes instruction and transformation first, and instruction and transformation take schools as foundation.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that rule rests first on moral instruction, and instruction rests on schools.

sentences.zh: 京師雖有太學，而天下學校未興。

translations.literal: Although the capital had the Imperial Academy, schools throughout the realm had not yet flourished.
translations.idiomatic: The capital had its academy, but schools across the empire had not yet taken root.

sentences.zh: 宜令郡縣皆立學校，延師儒，授生徒，講論聖道，使人日漸月化，以復先王之舊。

translations.literal: It is fitting to order every prefecture and county to establish schools, invite Confucian teachers, instruct students, expound the sage's Way, and let people be transformed day by day and month by month, restoring the institutions of the former kings.
translations.idiomatic: Every prefecture and county should establish schools, hire Confucian teachers, teach students the sage's Way, and restore the institutions of the ancient kings through steady daily cultivation.

sentences.zh: 」於是大建學校，府設教授，州設學正，縣設教諭，各一。

translations.literal: Thereupon schools were built on a grand scale: prefectures set professors, departments set directors of study, counties set instructors—one each.
translations.idiomatic: Schools then went up everywhere: one professor per prefecture, one director of study per department, and one instructor per county.

sentences.zh: 俱設訓導，府四，州三，縣二。

translations.literal: All also set assistant instructors: four in prefectures, three in departments, two in counties.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant instructors numbered four in prefectures, three in departments, and two in counties.

sentences.zh: 生員之數，府學四十人，州、縣以次減十。

translations.literal: The quota of students: forty in prefectural schools, with departments and counties reduced by ten in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Student quotas were forty per prefectural school, decreasing by ten at each lower level.

sentences.zh: 師生月廩食米，人六斗，有司給以魚肉。

translations.literal: Teachers and students received monthly grain rations of six dou per person, with fish and meat supplied by local officials.
translations.idiomatic: Teachers and students drew six dou of grain monthly, with fish and meat provided by local authorities.

sentences.zh: 學官月俸有差。

translations.literal: School officers' monthly salaries differed by rank.
translations.idiomatic: School officers were paid monthly salaries graded by rank.

sentences.zh: 生員專治一經，以禮、樂、射、禦、書、數設科分教，務求實才，頑不率者黜之。

translations.literal: Students specialized in one classic; rites, music, archery, charioteering, writing, and arithmetic were set as separate subjects for teaching, seeking real talent; the stubborn and noncompliant were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Students mastered one classic while rites, music, archery, charioteering, writing, and arithmetic were taught separately; the unteachable were expelled.

sentences.zh: 十五年，頒學規於國子監，又頒禁例十二條於天下，鐫立臥碑，置明倫堂之左。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, school regulations were promulgated at the Directorate, and twelve prohibitions were issued throughout the realm, carved on a stele placed to the left of the Hall of Bright Ethics.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 school rules were issued to the Directorate and twelve prohibitions were carved on a stele beside the Hall of Bright Ethics nationwide.

sentences.zh: 其不遵者，以違制論。

translations.literal: Those who did not comply were prosecuted for violating regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Violators were charged with breach of imperial regulation.

sentences.zh: 蓋無地而不設之學，無人而不納之教。

translations.literal: Truly there was no place without schools set up, no person without instruction received.
translations.idiomatic: No corner of the realm lacked a school; no subject went untaught.

sentences.zh: 庠聲序音，重規疊矩，無間於下邑荒徼，山陬海涯。

translations.literal: Academy sounds and ordered tones, rules layered upon rules, extended without gap to remote towns, mountain corners, and sea margins.
translations.idiomatic: School bells and ordered study reached even the remotest hamlets, mountain hollows, and seacoasts.

sentences.zh: 此明代學校之盛，唐、宋以來所不及也。

translations.literal: Such was the flourishing of Ming schools, unmatched since Tang and Song.
translations.idiomatic: Ming schools flourished as Tang and Song never had.

sentences.zh: 生員雖定數於國初，未幾即命增廣，不拘額數。

translations.literal: Although student quotas were fixed at the dynasty's founding, before long orders came to expand enrollment without limiting numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Initial student quotas were soon expanded without cap.

sentences.zh: 宣德中，定增廣之額：在京府學六十人，在外府學四十人，州、縣以次減十。

translations.literal: In the Xuande period, expanded quotas were fixed: sixty in capital prefectural schools, forty in outer prefectural schools, with departments and counties reduced by ten in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xuande expanded quotas were set at sixty for capital prefectures, forty elsewhere, and ten fewer at each lower level.

sentences.zh: 成化中，定衛學之例：四衛以上軍生八十人，三衛以上軍生六十人，二衛、一衛軍生四十人，有司儒學軍生二十人；

translations.literal: In the Chenghua period, guard-school rules were fixed: eighty military students in guards of four battalions or more, sixty in guards of three battalions or more, forty in guards of two or one battalion; civil prefectural and county schools twenty military students;
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua fixed guard-school quotas at eighty military students for four-battalion guards, sixty for three-battalion guards, forty for smaller guards, and twenty military students at civil prefectural and county schools;

sentences.zh: 土官子弟，許入附近儒學，無定額。

translations.literal: native-official sons were permitted to enter nearby Confucian schools with no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: sons of native officials could enroll in nearby Confucian schools without fixed quotas.

sentences.zh: 增廣既多，於是初設食廩者謂之廩膳生員，增廣者謂之增廣生員。

translations.literal: As expansion grew, those first receiving grain rations were called granary-stipend students, and those expanded were called expanded-enrollment students.
translations.idiomatic: Those first on grain stipends became granary-stipend students; added enrollees became expanded-enrollment students.

sentences.zh: 及其既久，人才愈多，又於額外增取，附於諸生之末，謂之附學生員。

translations.literal: After long years, as talent increased further, additional selections beyond the quota were attached at the end of the student rolls, called attached students.
translations.idiomatic: Over time extra selections beyond quota were appended to the rolls as attached students.

sentences.zh: 凡初入學者，止謂之附學，而廩膳、增廣，以歲科兩試等第高者補充之。

translations.literal: All who first entered were simply called attached students; granary-stipend and expanded-enrollment places were filled by those ranking highest in the annual and triennial examinations.
translations.idiomatic: New entrants began as attached students; granary-stipend and expanded slots went to top performers in annual and triennial exams.

sentences.zh: 非廩生久次者，不得充歲貢也。

translations.literal: Only granary-stipend students of long standing could qualify for annual tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Only long-serving granary-stipend students could be nominated for annual tribute.

sentences.zh: 士子未入學者，通謂之童生。

translations.literal: Scholars not yet enrolled in schools were generally called child scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Boys not yet enrolled were commonly called child scholars.

sentences.zh: 當大比之年，間收一二異敏，三場並通者，俾與諸生一體入場，謂之充場儒士。

translations.literal: In metropolitan examination years, one or two exceptionally sharp youths who passed all three sessions were allowed to enter the examination hall together with enrolled students, called examination-hall literati.
translations.idiomatic: In provincial exam years one or two precocious boys who passed all three sessions could sit with enrolled students as examination-hall literati.

sentences.zh: 中式即為舉人，不中式仍候提學官歲試，合格乃准入學。

translations.literal: If they passed they became provincial graduates; if not, they still awaited the education inspector's annual examination, and only after qualifying were they admitted to school.
translations.idiomatic: Passers became provincial graduates; failures waited for the education inspector's annual test before admission.

sentences.zh: 提學官在任三歲，兩試諸生。

translations.literal: Education inspectors, during three years in office, examined students twice.
translations.idiomatic: Education inspectors tested students twice during their three-year terms.

sentences.zh: 先以六等試諸生優劣，謂之歲考。

translations.literal: First they tested students' merit and defect in six grades, called the annual examination.
translations.idiomatic: First came the annual examination, ranking students in six grades.

sentences.zh: 一等前列者，視廩膳生有缺，依次充補，其次補增廣生。

translations.literal: Those in the front ranks of the first grade, when granary-stipend places were vacant, were filled in order; next came filling expanded-enrollment places.
translations.idiomatic: Top first-grade students filled vacant granary-stipend slots in order, then expanded-enrollment slots.

sentences.zh: 一二等皆給賞，三等如常，四等撻責，五等則廩、增遞降一等，附生降為青衣，六等黜革。

translations.literal: First and second grades all received rewards; third grade as usual; fourth grade received beating and reprimand; fifth grade demoted granary-stipend and expanded students one grade, attached students to blue-gown status; sixth grade expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Grades one and two earned rewards, three passed routinely, four brought beating, five demoted stipend or expanded students one rank and attached students to blue gowns, and six meant expulsion.

sentences.zh: 繼取一二等為科舉生員，俾應鄉試，謂之科考。

translations.literal: Next one or two grades were chosen as examination-recruitment students to sit the provincial examination, called the qualifying examination.
translations.idiomatic: The best one or two grades became examination-recruitment students for the provincial exam—the qualifying examination.

sentences.zh: 其充補廩、增給賞，悉如歲試。

translations.literal: Filling granary-stipend and expanded places and granting rewards all followed the annual examination.
translations.idiomatic: Stipend filling and rewards followed the same rules as the annual exam.

sentences.zh: 其等第仍分為六，而大抵多置三等。

translations.literal: The grades still divided into six, but for the most part many were placed in the third grade.
translations.idiomatic: Grades still ran to six, though most students landed in the third.

sentences.zh: 三等不得應鄉試，撻黜者僅百一，亦可絕無也。

translations.literal: Third grade could not sit the provincial examination; those beaten and expelled were barely one in a hundred, and sometimes there were none at all.
translations.idiomatic: Third-grade students could not sit the provincial exam; beatings and expulsions ran to perhaps one in a hundred, sometimes none.

sentences.zh: 生儒應試，每舉人一名，以科舉三十名為率。

translations.literal: When students sat examinations, for each provincial graduate thirty examination-recruitment students was the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial exams typically fielded thirty examination-recruitment students for each provincial graduate slot.

sentences.zh: 舉人屢廣額，科舉之數亦日增。

translations.literal: As provincial graduate quotas repeatedly expanded, examination-recruitment numbers also grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: As provincial quotas widened, examination-recruitment numbers rose steadily.

sentences.zh: 及求舉者益眾，又往往於定額之外加取，以收士心。

translations.literal: As candidates seeking advancement grew ever more numerous, supernumeraries were often added beyond the fixed quota to win scholars' loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: With more candidates competing, supernumeraries were often added beyond quota to win local goodwill.

sentences.zh: 凡督學者類然。

translations.literal: Education supervisors generally acted thus.
translations.idiomatic: Education supervisors commonly did the same.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十年，嘗下沙汰生員之令，御史楊宜爭之而止。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jiajing, an order to purge student rolls was once issued, but censor Yang Yi protested and it was halted.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 10 (1531) brought an order to cull student rolls, but censor Yang Yi's protest stopped it.

sentences.zh: 萬歷時，張居正當國，遂核減天下生員。

translations.literal: In the Wanli period, when Zhang Juzheng held power, student rolls throughout the realm were audited and reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wanli, with Zhang Juzheng in power, student rolls were audited and cut empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 督學官奉行太過，童生入學，有一州縣僅錄一人者，其科舉減殺可推而知也。

translations.literal: Education supervisors enforced this too harshly; in some prefectures and counties only one child scholar was admitted, and the reduction in examination-recruitment numbers can be inferred likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisors overshot the mark: some counties admitted only one child scholar, and examination-recruitment numbers shrank accordingly.

sentences.zh: 生員入學，初由巡按御史，布、按兩司及府州縣官。

translations.literal: At first student admission was handled by touring censors, provincial and surveillance commissioners, and prefectural, departmental, and county officials.
translations.idiomatic: Admission initially fell to touring censors, provincial and surveillance commissioners, and local officials.

sentences.zh: 正統元年始特置提學官，專使提督學政，南、北直隸俱御史，各省參用副使、僉事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengtong, education inspectors were specially established to supervise school administration; both metropolitan areas used censors, while provinces mixed vice commissioners and assistant commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengtong 1 (1436) created dedicated education inspectors: censors in both metropolises, vice and assistant commissioners in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年罷提學官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingtai, education inspectors were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtai 1 (1450) abolished the education inspectors.

sentences.zh: 天順六年復設，各賜敕諭十八條，俾奉行之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianshun they were restored, each granted an eighteen-article imperial instruction to be followed.
translations.idiomatic: Tianshun 6 (1462) restored them, each receiving an eighteen-article imperial instruction.

sentences.zh: 直省既設提學，有所轄太廣，及地最僻遠，歲巡所不能及者，乃酌其宜。

translations.literal: Once education inspectors were set up in the provinces, some jurisdictions were too broad, and places most remote where annual tours could not reach were handled as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial education inspectors covered vast territories; remote districts beyond annual reach were handled pragmatically.

sentences.zh: 口外及各都司、衛所、土官以屬分巡道員，直隸廬、鳳、淮、揚、滁、徐、和以屬江北巡按，湖廣衡、永、郴以屬湖南道，辰、靖以屬辰沅道，廣東瓊州以屬海南道，某肅衛所以屬巡按御史，亦皆專敕行事。

translations.literal: Areas beyond the passes and various regional military commissioners, guard posts, and native offices were assigned to circuit intendant officials; directly administered Luzhou, Fengyang, Huai'an, Yangzhou, Chuzhou, Xuzhou, and Hezhou to the Jiangbei touring censor; Hengyang, Yongzhou, and Chenzhou in Huguang to the Hunan circuit; Chenzhou and Jingzhou to the Chen-Yuan circuit; Qiongzhou in Guangdong to the Hainan circuit; Gansu guard posts to the touring censor—all also acted under separate imperial instructions.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the passes, regional commands, guard posts, and native offices fell to circuit intendants; Luzhou, Fengyang, Huai'an, Yangzhou, Chuzhou, Xuzhou, and Hezhou to the Jiangbei censor; Heng, Yong, and Chen to Hunan circuit; Chen and Jing to Chen-Yuan circuit; Qiongzhou to Hainan circuit; Gansu guard posts to the touring censor—all under separate imperial commissions.

sentences.zh: 萬曆四十一年，南直隸分上下江，湖廣分南北，始各增提學一員。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year of Wanli, southern Zhili was divided into upper and lower Jiang, and Huguang into north and south; each then gained one additional education inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 41 (1613) split southern Zhili into upper and lower Jiang and Huguang into north and south, each adding an education inspector.

sentences.zh: 提學之職，專督學校，不理刑名。

translations.literal: The duty of education inspectors was exclusively to supervise schools, not to handle criminal cases.
translations.idiomatic: Education inspectors supervised schools only and did not handle criminal matters.

sentences.zh: 所受詞訟，重者送按察司，輕者發有司，直隸則轉送巡按御史。

translations.literal: Petitions received: serious cases went to the surveillance commission, minor ones to local officials; in directly administered areas they were forwarded to the touring censor.
translations.idiomatic: Petitions they received: serious cases went to the surveillance commission, minor ones to local officials, and in metropolitan areas to the touring censor.

sentences.zh: 督、撫、巡按及布、按二司，亦不許侵提學職事也。

translations.literal: Governors-general, grand coordinators, touring censors, and provincial and surveillance commissioners were also not permitted to encroach on education inspectors' duties.
translations.idiomatic: Governors, coordinators, censors, and provincial commissioners likewise could not interfere in education affairs.

sentences.zh: 明初，優禮師儒，教官擢給事、御史，諸生歲貢者易得美官。

translations.literal: In the early Ming, Confucian teachers were greatly honored; instructors were promoted to supervising secretaries and censors, and students nominated through annual tribute easily obtained fine offices.
translations.idiomatic: Early Ming honored Confucian teachers, promoting instructors to secretaries and censors while tribute students often won good posts.

sentences.zh: 然鉗束亦甚謹。

translations.literal: Yet restraint was also very strict.
translations.idiomatic: Discipline, however, was equally strict.

sentences.zh: 太祖時，教官考滿，兼核其歲貢生員之數。

translations.literal: In the Taizu period, when instructors completed their term of service, the number of their annual tribute students was also audited.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Hongwu Emperor, instructors' performance reviews counted their annual tribute graduates.

sentences.zh: 後以歲貢為學校常例。

translations.literal: Later annual tribute became the standing practice of schools.
translations.idiomatic: Annual tribute later became schools' routine path to office.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，定學官考課法，專以科舉為殿最。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, the examination method for school officers was fixed, taking provincial graduates alone as the measure of merit.
translations.idiomatic: Year 26 fixed school officers' evaluations, ranking them solely by provincial graduates produced.

sentences.zh: 九年任滿，核其中式舉人，府九人、州六人、縣三人者為最。

translations.literal: After nine years in office, provincial graduates were audited: nine for prefectures, six for departments, and three for counties ranked highest.
translations.idiomatic: After nine years, prefectural instructors with nine provincial graduates, departmental with six, and county with three ranked highest.

sentences.zh: 其教官又考通經，即與升遷。

translations.literal: Instructors who also passed the classics examination were then promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Instructors who passed the classics exam were promoted.

sentences.zh: 舉人少者為平等，即考通經亦不遷。

translations.literal: Those with few provincial graduates ranked average; even if they passed the classics examination they were not transferred.
translations.idiomatic: Instructors with few graduates ranked average and were not promoted even after passing the classics exam.

sentences.zh: 舉人至少及全無者為殿，又考不通經，則黜降。

translations.literal: Those with the fewest provincial graduates and those with none ranked last; if they again failed the classics examination, they were demoted and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Instructors with the fewest provincial graduates—or none at all—ranked last, and those who also failed the classics exam were demoted or removed.

sentences.zh: 其待教官之嚴如此。

translations.literal: Such was the severity with which instructors were treated.
translations.idiomatic: Such were the strictures imposed on instructors.

sentences.zh: 生員入學十年，學無所成者，及有大過者，俱送部充吏，追奪廩糧。

translations.literal: Student scholars who had been enrolled ten years without achievement in learning, as well as those who had committed major offenses, were all sent to the ministry to serve as clerks, with their stipend grain reclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Students enrolled ten years without progress, or guilty of serious misconduct, were sent to the ministry as clerks and stripped of their grain stipends.

sentences.zh: 至正統十四年申明其制而稍更之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhengtong, the regulations were clarified and slightly altered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengtong 14 (1449) restated these rules with minor revisions.

sentences.zh: 受贓、奸盜、冒籍、宿娼、居喪娶妻妾所犯事理重者，直隸發充國子監膳夫，各省發充附近儒學膳夫、齋夫，滿日為民，俱追廩米。

translations.literal: Those whose offenses in accepting bribes, adultery and theft, false registration, lodging with prostitutes, or taking wives and concubines during mourning were of serious gravity: in directly administered areas they were sent to serve as kitchen workers at the Imperial Academy, in provinces as kitchen and service workers at nearby Confucian schools; when their term was complete they became commoners, and all stipend grain was reclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Serious offenses—bribery, theft, false registration, patronizing brothels, marrying during mourning—meant kitchen or service work at the Imperial Academy in the metropolises or at nearby Confucian schools in the provinces; after completing their term they returned to commoner status, with stipends forfeited.

sentences.zh: 犯輕充吏者，不追廩米。

translations.literal: Those assigned to serve as clerks for minor offenses did not have stipend grain reclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Minor offenders demoted to clerical service did not forfeit their grain stipends.

sentences.zh: 其待諸生之嚴又如此。

translations.literal: Such too was the severity with which students were treated.
translations.idiomatic: Students faced discipline equally stringent.

sentences.zh: 然其後教官之黜降，生員之充發，皆廢格不行，即臥碑亦具文矣。

translations.literal: Yet afterward the demotion and dismissal of instructors and the assignment of student scholars were all abolished and went unenforced; even the stone tablets set up for the purpose became empty formalities.
translations.idiomatic: Later, however, instructor demotions and student punishments lapsed entirely; even the commemorative stone tablets became dead letters.

sentences.zh: 諸生上者中式，次者廩生，年久充貢，或選拔為貢生。

translations.literal: Among students, the foremost passed the examinations; the next became stipendiary students; after many years they served as tribute, or were selected and promoted as tribute students.
translations.idiomatic: Top students passed the exams; others became stipendiary students, and after long service advanced as tribute scholars or were selected for tribute nomination.

sentences.zh: 其累試不第、年逾五十、願告退閑者，給與冠帶，仍復其身。

translations.literal: Those who repeatedly failed the examinations, were over fifty years of age, and wished to retire in leisure were given caps and sashes, restoring their personal status.
translations.idiomatic: Students who repeatedly failed, passed fifty, and sought retirement received caps and sashes and regained commoner status.

sentences.zh: 其後有納粟馬捐監之例，則諸生又有援例而出學者矣。

translations.literal: Later there were precedents for donating grain and horses to purchase supervisory student status, and so among students there were also those who relied on such precedents to leave the schools.
translations.idiomatic: Later, grain-and-horse purchase routes to supervisory status also let students leave school by precedent.

sentences.zh: 提學官歲試校文之外，令教官舉諸生行優劣者一二人，賞黜之以為勸懲。

translations.literal: Beyond the education inspector's annual examinations and essay review, instructors were ordered to recommend one or two students distinguished by conduct, good or bad, and reward or punish them as encouragement and warning.
translations.idiomatic: Besides annual exams, education inspectors had instructors recommend one or two students for conduct, rewarding or penalizing them as examples.

sentences.zh: 此其大較也。

translations.literal: This, in broad outline, was the system.
translations.idiomatic: Such, in broad outline, was the arrangement.

sentences.zh: 諸生應試之文，通謂之舉業。

translations.literal: The essays submitted by students for examinations were generally called examination compositions.
translations.idiomatic: Examination essays by students were collectively called juye, "examination compositions."

sentences.zh: 《四書》義一道，二百字以上。

translations.literal: One essay on the meaning of the Four Books, of more than two hundred characters.
translations.idiomatic: One Four Books essay of at least two hundred characters.

sentences.zh: 經義一道，三百字以上。

translations.literal: One classic exegesis essay, of more than three hundred characters.
translations.idiomatic: One classic exegesis of at least three hundred characters.

sentences.zh: 取書旨明晰而已，不尚華採也。

translations.literal: What was sought was merely clarity of the text's meaning; ornate style was not valued.
translations.idiomatic: Clarity of meaning was valued; ornate flourishes were not.

sentences.zh: 其後標新領異，益漓厥初。

translations.literal: Later, striving for novelty led ever further from the original standards.
translations.idiomatic: Later writers prized novelty, drifting further from the original standards.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十五年，禮部言：「唐文初尚靡麗而士趨浮薄，宋文初尚鉤棘而人習險譎。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Wanli, the Ministry of Rites said: "Tang prose at first prized elegance and splendor, and scholars turned frivolous and shallow; Song prose at first prized barbed difficulty, and people grew crafty and deceitful.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 15 (1587), the Ministry of Rites reported: "Early Tang prose favored elegance, and writers grew frivolous; early Song prose favored knotty difficulty, and writers grew devious.

sentences.zh: 國初舉業有用六經語者，其後引《左傳》、《國語》矣，又引《史記》、《漢書》矣。

translations.literal: In examination compositions of the early dynasty, there were those who used language from the Six Classics; afterward they cited the Zuo Commentary and Discourses of the States; then they cited the Records of the Grand Historian and Book of Han as well.
translations.idiomatic: Early Ming exam essays drew on the Six Classics; later writers cited the Zuo Commentary and Discourses of the States, then the Records of the Grand Historian and Book of Han.

sentences.zh: 《史記》窮而用六子，六子窮而用百家，甚至佛經、《道藏》摘而用之，流弊安窮。

translations.literal: When the Records of the Grand Historian was exhausted, they turned to the Six Masters; when the Six Masters was exhausted, they turned to the hundred schools; some even excerpted Buddhist scriptures and the Daoist Canon for use—how could the harm ever end?
translations.idiomatic: Once the Historical Records were mined out, writers turned to the Six Masters; once those were exhausted, to the hundred schools—and some even plundered Buddhist scriptures and the Daoist Canon. Where would such excess stop?

sentences.zh: 弘治、正德、嘉靖初年，中式文字純正典雅。

translations.literal: In the early years of Hongzhi, Zhengde, and Jiajing, successful examination essays were pure, correct, and elegant.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi, Zhengde, and early Jiajing essays were pure and elegant.

sentences.zh: 宜選其尤者，刊佈學宮，俾知趨向。

translations.literal: The finest among them should be selected, printed and distributed to academies, so that students would know the proper direction.
translations.idiomatic: The best should be published at academies as models of proper style.

sentences.zh: 」因取中式文字一百十餘篇，奏請刊佈，以為準則。

translations.literal: Accordingly more than one hundred and ten successful examination essays were selected, memorialized for printing and distribution, to serve as standards.
translations.idiomatic: More than 110 successful essays were submitted for publication as official models.

sentences.zh: 時方崇尚新奇，厭薄先民矩矱，以士子所好為趨，不遵上指也。

translations.literal: At the time novelty was in vogue; the measures and compasses of earlier generations were despised; scholars followed their own tastes and did not obey the court's direction.
translations.idiomatic: But novelty was in fashion; scholars scorned older models and followed their own tastes rather than imperial guidance.

sentences.zh: 啟、禎之間，文體益變，以出入經史百氏為高，而恣軼者亦多矣。

translations.literal: Between the Tianqi and Chongzhen reigns, examination style changed further; to move freely through the classics, histories, and various schools was held lofty, and unrestrained excess became common.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianqi and Chongzhen, style shifted again: fluency across classics, histories, and schools was prized, and many wrote with reckless abandon.

sentences.zh: 雖數申詭異險僻之禁，勢重難返，卒不能從。

translations.literal: Although the prohibitions against bizarre, eccentric, and abstruse writing were reiterated many times, the momentum was heavy and hard to reverse; in the end none could comply.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated bans on bizarre and abstruse writing could not turn the tide; compliance proved impossible.

sentences.zh: 論者以明舉業文字比唐人之詩，國初比初唐，成、弘、正、嘉比盛唐，隆、萬比中唐，啟、禎比晚唐云。

translations.literal: Commentators compared Ming examination compositions to Tang poetry: the early dynasty to Early Tang, the Chenghua-Hongzhi-Zhengde-Jiajing periods to High Tang, the Longqing-Wanli periods to Middle Tang, and the Tianqi-Chongzhen periods to Late Tang, they say.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators likened Ming exam essays to Tang poetry—Early Ming to Early Tang; Chenghua, Hongzhi, Zhengde, and Jiajing to High Tang; Longqing and Wanli to Middle Tang; and Tianqi and Chongzhen to Late Tang.

sentences.zh: 自儒學外，又有宗學、社學、武學。

translations.literal: Apart from Confucian schools, there were also clan schools, community schools, and military schools.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond Confucian academies, the dynasty also maintained clan schools, community schools, and military schools.

sentences.zh: 宗學之設，世子、長子、眾子、將軍、中尉年未弱冠者俱與焉。

translations.literal: In establishing clan schools, heir apparents, eldest sons, younger sons, generals, and assistant commandants all not yet having reached the capping age participated.
translations.idiomatic: Clan schools enrolled imperial clansmen—heir apparents, eldest sons, younger sons, generals, and assistant commandants—before they came of age.

sentences.zh: 其師，於王府長史、紀善、伴讀、教授等官擇學行優長者除授。

translations.literal: Their teachers were selected from among palace chancellors, recorders, reading companions, and instructors for excellence in learning and conduct, and appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Teachers were drawn from palace chancellors, recorders, reading companions, and instructors for distinguished learning and conduct.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中，定宗室子十歲以上，俱入宗學。

translations.literal: In the Wanli period, it was fixed that imperial clansmen aged ten and above all entered clan schools.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli rules required all clansmen aged ten or older to enter clan schools.

sentences.zh: 若宗子眾多，分置數師，或於宗室中推舉一人為宗正，領其事。

translations.literal: If clansmen were numerous, several teachers were assigned separately, or one person was recommended from among the imperial clan as clan director to oversee the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Where clansmen were numerous, schools hired multiple teachers or appointed a clan director from among the royal family.

sentences.zh: 令學生誦習《皇明祖訓》、《孝順事實》、《為善陰騭》諸書，而《四書》、《五經》、《通鑒》、性理亦相兼誦讀。

translations.literal: Students were ordered to recite and study such books as the Ancestral Instructions of the August Ming, Records of Filial Devotion, and Hidden Merits of Doing Good, while the Four Books, Five Classics, Comprehensive Mirror, and Neo-Confucian learning were also read together.
translations.idiomatic: Students memorized the Ancestral Instructions, Records of Filial Devotion, Hidden Merits of Doing Good, alongside the Four Books, Five Classics, Comprehensive Mirror, and Neo-Confucian texts.

sentences.zh: 尋復增宗副二人。

translations.literal: Soon two additional deputy clan directors were added.
translations.idiomatic: Two deputy clan directors were soon added.

sentences.zh: 子弟入學者，每歲就提學官考試，衣冠一如生員。

translations.literal: Clansmen enrolled in the schools were examined each year by the education inspector, their caps and robes the same as student scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Enrolled clansmen took annual exams before education inspectors, dressed like regular students.

sentences.zh: 已復令一體鄉試，許得中式。

translations.literal: Later they were also ordered to take the provincial examinations together with others, and were permitted to pass.
translations.idiomatic: They were later allowed to sit the provincial exams and pass.

sentences.zh: 其後宗學浸多，頗有致身兩榜、起家翰林者。

translations.literal: Later clan schools gradually multiplied, and quite a few attained both examination lists or rose from the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Clan schools proliferated, and some graduates reached both provincial and metropolitan lists or entered the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 社學，自洪武八年，延師以教民間子弟，兼讀《御製大誥》及本朝律令。

translations.literal: Community schools, beginning in the eighth year of Hongwu, engaged teachers to instruct commoners' children, who also read the Imperial Great Announcements and the dynasty's laws and statutes.
translations.idiomatic: From Hongwu 8 (1375), community schools hired teachers for commoners' children, who also studied the Imperial Great Announcements and dynastic law.

sentences.zh: 正統時，許補儒學生員。

translations.literal: In the Zhengtong period, they were permitted to fill vacancies as Confucian school student scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengtong rules allowed graduates to fill student-scholar vacancies at Confucian schools.

sentences.zh: 弘治十七年，令各府、州、縣建立社學，選擇明師，民間幼童十五以下者送入讀書，講習冠、婚、喪、祭之禮。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Hongzhi, each prefecture, department, and county was ordered to establish community schools, select capable teachers, and send common children fifteen and under to study, lecturing on the rites of capping, marriage, mourning, and sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 17 (1504) ordered every prefecture, department, and county to open community schools, hire teachers, and enroll common children under fifteen to study capping, marriage, mourning, and sacrifice rites.

sentences.zh: 然其法久廢，浸不舉行。

translations.literal: Yet the regulations long fell into disuse and were gradually not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The system long lapsed and was barely enforced.

sentences.zh: 武學之設，自洪武時置大寧等衛儒學，教武官子弟。

translations.literal: The establishment of military schools began in the Hongwu period with Confucian schools at guards such as Daming, to teach the sons of military officers.
translations.idiomatic: Military schooling began under Hongwu with Confucian academies at guards like Daming for officers' sons.

sentences.zh: 正統中，成國公硃勇奏選驍勇都指揮等官五十一員，熟嫻騎射幼官一百員，始命兩京建武學以訓誨之。

translations.literal: In the Zhengtong period, the Cheng State Duke Zhu Yong memorialized selecting fifty-one valiant battalion commanders and the like, and one hundred junior officers skilled in horsemanship and archery; only then were military schools ordered built in both capitals to instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhengtong, Cheng State Duke Zhu Yong proposed fifty-one seasoned battalion commanders and one hundred junior officers skilled in horsemanship and archery as instructors, prompting military schools in both capitals.

sentences.zh: 尋命都司、衛所應襲子弟年十歲以上者，提學官選送武學讀書，無武學者送衛學或附近儒學。

translations.literal: Soon heirs apparent to regional commands and guard posts aged ten and above were ordered to be selected and sent by education inspectors to military schools for study; where there were no military schools, they were sent to guard schools or nearby Confucian schools.
translations.idiomatic: Heirs to regional commands and guard posts aged ten or older were sent by education inspectors to military schools—or to guard schools or nearby Confucian academies where none existed.

sentences.zh: 成化中，敕所司歲終考試入學武生。

translations.literal: In the Chenghua period, relevant offices were commanded to examine military students at year's end.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua orders required annual year-end exams for military students.

sentences.zh: 十年以上學無可取者，追廩還官，送營操練。

translations.literal: Those who after more than ten years had nothing worth taking from their learning had their stipends reclaimed and were returned to office, sent to camps for drill and training.
translations.idiomatic: After ten years without merit, stipends were reclaimed and students returned to camp for drill.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，從兵部尚書馬文升言，刑《武經七書》分散兩京武學及應襲舍人。

translations.literal: In the Hongzhi period, following Minister of War Ma Wensheng's proposal, the Seven Military Classics were engraved and printed, distributed to military schools in both capitals and to heir apparent retainers.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi, heeding Minister of War Ma Wensheng, engraved and distributed the Seven Military Classics to both capitals' military schools and heir retainers.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，移京城東武學於皇城西隅廢寺，俾大小武官子弟及勳爵新襲者，肄業其中，用文武重臣教習。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing period, the eastern capital military school was moved to an abandoned temple at the western corner of the imperial city, so that sons of military officers high and low and those newly inheriting noble ranks might study there, with eminent civil and military officials as teachers.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing relocated the eastern capital military school to a disused temple west of the palace, enrolling officers' sons and newly ennobled heirs under senior civil and military instructors.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中，兵部言，武庫司專設主事一員管理武學，近者裁去，請復專設。

translations.literal: In the Wanli period, the Ministry of War reported that the Bureau of the Military Storehouse had specially established one director to administer military schools, but this had recently been cut; they requested that the dedicated post be restored.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli, the Ministry of War noted that a dedicated Military Storehouse director had overseen military schools until recently cut, and asked that the post be restored.

sentences.zh: 教官升堂，都指揮執弟子禮，請遵《會典》例，立為程式。

translations.literal: When instructors ascended the hall, battalion commanders performed the rites of disciples; they requested that the precedent in the Collected Statutes be followed and established as standard procedure.
translations.idiomatic: Battalion commanders observed disciple rites when instructors taught; they asked that Collected Statutes precedent become formal procedure.

sentences.zh: 詔皆如議。

translations.literal: An edict approved all as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved every proposal.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十年，令天下府、州、縣學皆設武學生員，提學官一體考取。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Chongzhen, all prefectural, departmental, and county schools throughout the realm were ordered to establish military student scholars, examined together by education inspectors.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 10 (1637) ordered every prefecture, department, and county to enroll military students, examined by education inspectors alongside civil students.

sentences.zh: 已又申《會典》事例，簿記功能，有不次擢用、黜退、送操、獎罰、激厲之法。

translations.literal: Then the precedents in the Collected Statutes were again proclaimed: records were kept of merit, with methods for extraordinary promotion, dismissal, sending to drill, rewards and punishments, and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Collected Statutes procedures were reaffirmed—merit registers, exceptional promotion, dismissal, drill assignment, rewards, punishments, and incentives.

sentences.zh: 時事方棘，無所益也。

translations.literal: Affairs of the time were already critical; it benefited nothing.
translations.idiomatic: But times were desperate, and none of it availed.
